OVERVIEW
Who We Are
We are a leading pure-play foundry specializing in 12-inch wafer manufacturing,
operating at a critical juncture of the global semiconductor value chain. As dedicated wafer
fabricationserviceproviders,foundriestranslateICdesignblueprintsfromfabless,fabliteand
integrated device manufacturer (“IDM”) companies into high-quality processed wafers at
scale.
Since inception, we have focused on the advancement of process technologies. Our
foundry services cover technology nodes ranging from 150nm to 40nm, with the 28nm Logic
IC platform successfully developed as of the Latest Practicable Date, positioning us to
address evolving demand for higher-performance and more power-efficient semiconductor
solutions. Our process capabilities are centered on key application-specific IC categories,
including display driver ICs (“DDIC”) that enable display control, complementary
metal-oxide-semiconductor image sensors (“CIS”) that enable image sensing, and power
management ICs (“PMIC”) that regulate and optimize power usage. Our Logic ICs, which
support data processing, and microcontroller units (“MCU”), which provide embedded
control, have also scaled rapidly during the Track Record Period. Leveraging this portfolio,
we are able to support a broad spectrum of applications across consumer electronics,
automotiveelectronics,industrialcontrol,artificialintelligence(“AI”),theInternetof Things
(“IoT”) and memory.
Our ability to combine differentiated process technologies with stable manufacturing
scale has strengthened our position in the global foundry landscape. From 2020 to 2025, we
achieved the fastest growth in production capacity and revenue among the global top ten
wafer foundries, according to Frost & Sullivan. In 2025, we ranked as the ninth largest wafer
foundry worldwide and the third largest in Chinese Mainland by revenue, according to the
same source.

Our Business Model
The wafer foundry industry constitutes a critical pillar of the global semiconductor
value chain. Based on upstream supply of essential materials and technologies including
silicon wafers, photoresists, specialty chemicals, core equipment, electronic design
automation tools and intellectual property licensing, wafer foundries provide specialized
wafer fabrication services for IC design companies, including fabless, fablite and IDM
companies, manufacturing their IC design blueprints into processed wafers with quality at
scale. While fabless companies fully outsource wafer fabrication to wafer foundries, fablite
andIDMcompanieswithin-houseICmanufacturingcapabilitiesmayalsopartnerwithwafer
foundries to access specialized technologies, secure stable production capacity and enhance
cost effectiveness. These processed wafers are further delivered to IC design companies for
packagingandtestingbyOutsourcedSemiconductorAssemblyandTest(“OSAT”)providers,
which are then integrated by IC design companies into end products across a wide range of
applications such as consumer electronics, automotive electronics, industrial control, AI, the
IoT and memory.
Within this value chain, we operate as a pure-play 12-inch wafer foundry, bridging
technology development with large-scale manufacturing to deliver power-efficient,
high-performanceICs.Ourtechnologyplatformportfoliooffersfabricationservicesprimarily
including DDIC, CIS and PMIC, with Logic IC and MCU scaling rapidly during the Track
RecordPeriod.WeserveadiversifiedcustomerbasecomprisingleadingICdesigncompanies,
including fabless, fablite and IDM companies, across end markets including consumer
electronics, automotive electronics, smart home, industrial control, AI, the IoT and memory.
– 2 –

=== PAGE 12 ===
SUMMARY
In wafer fabrication, silicon wafer sizes have evolved from the initial 6-inch and 8-inch
formatstothecurrentmainstream12-inch.While8-inchproductionlinescontinuetosupport
legacy applications, incremental capacity growth now primarily stems from 12-inch wafers,
which, with a surface area approximately 2.25 times that of 8-inch wafers, offer significantly
higherdieoutputandenhancedcostperwaferatthesameyield.Specializingin12-inchwafer
fabrication, we achieve high integration density, compact component design and superior
electrical performance.
The level of technological sophistication in wafer fabrication services is typically
reflected by process technology nodes. According to Frost & Sullivan, leading-edge nodes at
or below 7nm are used in high-performance processors, AI accelerators, flagship smartphone
system-on-chips (“SOC”) and advanced networking chips to address compute-intensive logic
tasks. Advanced nodes ranging from 10nm to 22nm are typically adopted for applications
requiringbalancedperformanceandintegration,suchasmid-rangeconsumerSOCs,high-end
MCU, CIS and PMIC designs. Downstream applications such as industrial control, the IoT,
display and power devices generally have a sustained and stringent requirement of
semiconductorproductsforlong-termreliabilityandoperationalrobustness,whichunderpins
the continued and widespread adoption of mature nodes at 28nm and above. For critical
componentsincludingDDIC,CIS,PMICsandMCUs,maturenodesarewidelypreferreddue
to their well-established and extensively validated manufacturing processes. Chips fabricated
using such mature node technologies typically feature thicker gate oxide layers, which help
reduce electric field intensity and enhance voltage tolerance. Their relatively longer
conductive channels further contribute to stable electrical performance under variations in
temperature and operating voltage. In addition, mature node platforms often incorporate
dedicated high-voltage device structures designed to effectively distribute electrical stress,
thereby materially improving device reliability over extended operating lifecycles. These
inherent technical attributes make mature nodes a natural choice for safety-critical and
high-voltage applications, sustaining robust market demand. In addition, industry
performance is commonly assessed based on key operational metrics including wafer sales
volume,productioncapacityandyieldrate.Ourcomprehensiveportfolioof waferfabrication
services cover technology nodes that had positioned us as one of the leaders among domestic
peers across multiple product categories, reaching 40nm for DDIC, 55nm for CIS and Logic
IC and 110nm for PMIC and MCU as of the Latest Practicable Date, according to the same
source.
By integrating process expertise, yield optimization and cost discipline, we provide a
manufacturingplatformthatenablescustomerstoaccelerateproductcycles,ensureconsistent
quality and achieve scalable production. With localized operations, we further reinforce our
position as a trusted foundry partner by helping customers mitigate supply chain risks and
maintain stability and certainty in their operations.
Our Technology Capabilities
Wehaveestablishedmassproductioncapabilitiesacrosstechnologynodesrangingfrom
150nm to 40nm. Our fabrication expertise extends across a diverse portfolio of technology
platforms encompassing DDIC, CIS, PMIC, Logic IC and MCU, forming a comprehensive
and differentiated technology portfolio that supports our leading position in key market
segments.Tofurtheroptimizeourportfolio,wemaintainaconsistentfocusontheupgradeof
processtechnologies.Asof theLatestPracticableDate,wehadcommencedpilotrunof 28nm
Logic IC and achieved mass production of 40nm high-voltage organic light-emitting diode
displaydriverintegratedcircuit(“OLEDDDIC”)(atypeof DDICdesignedtocontrolOLED
panels with higher precision and power efficiency), 55nm mid-to-high-end backside
illumination (“BSI”) image sensors (a type of CIS featuring a sensor architecture that allows
light to enter from the back side of the silicon substrate to enhance sensitivity and
performance) and 55nm full-process stacked CIS (which integrates multiple sensor layers
verticallytoimproveimagequalityandfunctionality),withdevelopmentof other28nmwafer
fabrication solutions such as OLED DDIC progressing steadily.

Our Financial Performance
We have consistently demonstrated resilient performance amid industry cycles during
theTrackRecordPeriod.In2023,2024and2025,ourtotalrevenueamountedtoRMB7,182.7
million, RMB9,119.6 million and RMB10,388.3 million, respectively, with the gross profit
margins of 20.3%, 25.2% and 22.7% in the same respective years. Our net profit was
RMB119.2 million, RMB482.2 million and RMB466.5 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025,
respectively, with the net profit margins of 1.7%, 5.3% and 4.5% in the same respective years.
In recent years, the global wafer foundry industry has experienced sustained long-term
growth, alongside normal cyclical adjustments. Following a surge in downstream
semiconductor demand in 2021 and 2022 driven by post-pandemic recovery and supply chain
tightness, the industry entered a phase of inventory normalization in 2023, as customers
across the semiconductor value chain focused on digesting elevated inventory levels amid
softer demand from consumer electronics. Notwithstanding this temporary adjustment, the
global wafer foundry market continued to expand overall, growing from approximately
US$100.2billionin2021toUS$174.7billionin2025,representingaCAGRof 14.9%.Against
this backdrop, our revenue increased from 2023 to 2025, primarily driven by an increase in
market demand, an improved product mix and enhanced economies of scale. As advised by
Frost & Sullivan, our Directors believe that our financial performance remained broadly
stable and in line with overall market dynamics. On such basis, nothing has come to the
attention of the Sole Sponsor that would cause the Sole Sponsor to disagree with the
Directors’view.
Looking forward, our Directors believe that demand in the semiconductor market will
remain robust, particularly within the mature-node segment in which we operate. Supportive
government policies and structurally expanding downstream applications are expected to
underpinstableindustrydevelopment.Inparticular,growthinautomotiveelectronics,AIand
robotics continues to increase semiconductor content per device, with PMICs, MCUs and
DDICs predominantly manufactured on mature nodes, supporting sustained demand and
healthy supply-demand dynamics. See “Industry Overview — Global Wafer Foundry
Market.”

Overview

fabrication, concentrated within a single manufacturing campus located in Hefei, Anhui
Province. As of December 31, 2025, the production base had a total gross floor area of

andPMIC,withLogicICandMCUscalingrapidlyduringtheTrackRecordPeriod.Building
ondiversetechnologynodesspanningfrom150nmto28nm,eachplatformisconfiguredwith

transistors, embedded non-volatile memory and imaging structures, to address the functional
requirements of different end applications and enhance product performance, cost efficiency
and design flexibility. These platforms form the foundation of our foundry services, enabling
us to deliver optimal power performance, enhanced processing speed, integration density and
manufacturability across a broad range of applications.

Unaudited Financial Information for the Three Months Ended March 31, 2026
Our revenue increased by 10.3% from RMB2,543.2 million in the three months ended
March 31, 2025 to RMB2,806.1 million in the three months ended March 31, 2026, primarily
due to increased sales volume of wafers, mainly comprising PMIC, DDIC and MCU.
Our cost of sales increased by 17.7% from RMB1,897.5 million in the three months
ended March 31, 2025 to RMB2,232.6 million in the three months ended March 31, 2026,
primarily driven by higher production costs associated with increased sales volume of wafers
as well as higher depreciation costs for relevant production facilities in line with our capacity
ramp-up.
As a result of the foregoing, our gross profit decreased by 11.2% from RMB645.7
million in the three months ended March 31, 2025 to RMB573.5 million in the three months
ended March 31, 2026. Our gross profit margin decreased from 25.4% to 20.4%, primarily
attributable to (i) short-term pricing pressure on our products as a result of intensified
industry competition and (ii) increased depreciation of production facilities in line with our
capacity ramp-up.
Our net profit decreased by 66.8% from RMB85.8 million in the three months ended
March 31, 2025 to RMB28.5 million in the three months ended March 31, 2026, primarily
attributable to (i) the decrease in our gross profit for the reasons set out above and (ii) the
increase of fair value losses in listed equity instruments led by share price fluctuations.
Our total assets remained relatively stable at RMB53,298.0 million as of December 31,
2025 and RMB54,705.9 million as of March 31, 2026. Our total liabilities remained relatively
stable at RMB25,210.3 million as of December 31, 2025 and RMB24,946.7 million as of
March31,2026.Ournetassetsincreasedby6.0%fromRMB28,087.7millionasof December

TARIFF, TRADE RESTRICTION AND EXPORT CONTROL IMPLICATIONS
U.S. Tariff Implications
On December 23, 2025, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (“USTR”)
announced that it would increase tariffs on Chinese semiconductor imports, with an initial
tariff level of zero, increasing in 18 months on June 23, 2027, to a rate to be announced not
fewer than 30 days prior to that date (the “Section 301 Tariff”). Separately, since February 1,
2025, President Trump imposed additional tariffs on all imports from China. Following the
ruling of the U.S. Supreme Court and pursuant to the relevant executive orders and official
notices issued by the U.S. government, the tariffs previously imposed under the International
Emergency Economic Powers Act (“IEEPA”) became inactive on February 24, 2026. In lieu
thereof,atemporary10%tariff wasimposedunderSection122of theTradeActof 1974fora
period of 150 days. Accordingly, as of the Latest Practicable Date, a 10% tariff applies to
goodsimportedintotheUnitedStatesfromChinaafterrevokingthetariffsundertheIEEPA
effective on February 24, 2026. Such tariff arrangement is temporary in nature and remains
subject to further regulatory developments and policy changes.
As advised by our U.S. Export Control and Sanctions Legal Advisor, considering that
(i) during the Track Record Period, we did not have any direct export to the U.S., and to the
best of our knowledge, we did not have any indirect sales to the U.S. either; and (ii) since the
impositionof theTariffs,noneof ourcustomershadcanceledtheirorderswithus,norhadwe
experienced any material adverse changes in our order volume, product price, customer
paymentorlogisticsarrangementsduetotheU.S.Tariffsissue,notariffshavebeenpassedon
to customers and our Directors do not expect the U.S. Tariffs to have any direct or indirect
material adverse impact on our business operations or financial performance.
U.S. Export Control Implications
Under the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (“EAR”), a license from the U.S.
Department of Commerce, Bureau of Industry and Security (“BIS”) may be required for the
export, re-export or in-country transfer of any items (including commodities, software, and
technology) subject to the EAR. Items subject to the EAR include not only those made in or
located within the United States, but also certain foreign-made items. In addition, recent
developments under the EAR, including the “Supercomputer and Semiconductor
Manufacturing End-Use” restrictions, among others, are designed to limit China’s access to
advanced computing and semiconductor manufacturing technologies. Effective from October
2022,Section744.23of theEARimposeslicenserequirementswhereanexporter,re-exporter,
ortransferorknowsorhasreasontoknowthatcertainEAR-controlleditemsareintendedfor
supercomputer or semiconductor manufacturing end-uses, with implementation phased in
over time.
AsadvisedbyourU.S.ExportControlandSanctionsLegalAdvisor,giventhenatureof
theitemsweprocure,theproductswemanufacture,andtheirintendedend-uses,ourDirectors
believe that the Supercomputer and Semiconductor Manufacturing End-Use restrictions are
unlikelytohaveamaterialadverseimpactonourbusinessoperations.Inaddition,asadvised
by our U.S. Export Control and Sanctions Legal Advisor, our Group was not included on the
U.S. Entity List or any other U.S. export control restriction lists as of the Latest Practicable
Date. During the Track Record Period, we did not experience any significant difficulties in
procuring production materials from the U.S. or other jurisdictions. Our suppliers have not
notified us of any changes or disruptions to supply arrangements. Our procurement, R&D
and expansion activities have proceeded normally.

IMPACT OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
On January 30, 2020, the International Health Regulations Emergency Committee of
the World Health Organization declared the novel coronavirus disease 2019 (the
“COVID-19”) outbreak a public health emergency of international concern, and on March
11,2020,theWorldHealthOrganizationdeclaredtheglobalCOVID-19outbreakapandemic.
During 2022, demand for electronic products such as computers and tablets increased
significantly, driven by remote working and online learning needs, which in turn supported
higher order volumes and pricing, particularly in the DDIC foundry segment. Following this
periodof elevateddemand,thesemiconductormarketenteredapost-pandemicnormalization
phase in 2023, as downstream customers adjusted inventory levels and demand dynamics
returned to more normalized patterns. See “Industry Overview — Global Wafer Foundry
Market — The Size of Global Integrated Circuit Market.”

GLOSSARY OF TECHNICAL TERMS
Thisglossaryof technicaltermscontainsexplanationsof certaintechnicaltermsused
in this prospectus in connection with our Company and our business. Such terminology and
meanings may not correspond to standard industry meanings or usages of those terms.
“5G” the fifth-generation wireless technology standard that
aims to provide significantly faster data speeds, lower
latency, and greater connectivity compared to previous
generations of mobile networks
“advanced process” A newer, smaller-geometry semiconductor process node
designed to achieve higher performance, lower power
consumption, and greater density, but typically with
higher cost and complexity
“AEC-Q” a set of automotive quality and reliability standards
defined by the Automotive Electronics Council (AEC)
for qualifying electronic components used in vehicles
“analog module” a circuit block that processes continuous electrical
signals, typically used for amplification, filtering, or
signal conversion in mixed-signal or sensor applications
“BCD” bipolar-CMOS-DMOS, a key process technology for
power ICs. it is a family of silicon processes, each of
which combines the strengths of three different process
technologies onto a single chip: bipolar for precise
analog functions, CMOS (complementary
metal-oxide-semiconductor) for digital design and
DMOS(doublediffusedmetaloxidesemiconductor)for
power and high-voltage elements
“bit” the smallest unit of data in computing, representing a
binary value of 0 or 1
“BSI” backside illumination image sensor, a type of CIS with
sensor architecture where light enters from the back side
of the silicon substrate to improve the sensitivity and
performance of image sensors
“CIS” complementary metal-oxide semiconductor image
sensor
“CMOS” complementary metal-oxide semiconductor, an
integrated circuit that incorporates negative channel
(n-channel)andpositivechannel(p-channel)transistors
“CPU” central processing unit, the main processing unit in
computing systems to execute instructions, manage
systemoperationsandcoordinatetasksacrosshardware
and software
“crystal lattice damage” structural defects in the atomic arrangement of a
semiconductor crystal that can affect device
performance

=== PAGE 39 ===
GLOSSARY OF TECHNICAL TERMS
“customer retention rate” the revenue generated in the previous year from
customers who also contributed revenue in the current
year, divided by our total revenue in the previous year
“DDIC” display driver integrated circuit, a type of IC
responsible for processing signals and precisely
controlling the operation of advanced display panels
“EDA” electronic design automation, software tools used for
designing and verifying integrated circuits
“embedded non-volatile memory” memory integrated within a chip that retains data even
when power is removed
“full-process stacked CIS” a CMOS image sensor architecture in which the pixel
layer and logic processing layer are vertically stacked
using advanced wafer bonding technology, in order to
enhance image quality and performance
“GPU” graphics processing unit, a specialized electronic circuit
designed to accelerate the processing of images and
videos, as well as complex mathematical calculations,
which is typically used to enhance graphics rendering,
support AI applications and improve overall
computational efficiency
“high-voltage transistor” a transistor designed to operate at elevated voltage
levels for power applications
“I/O Interface” Input/Output Interface, the communication channel
that connects a computing or control system with
externaldevices,enablingdatainput,output,andsignal
exchange
“IATF16949” a global quality management standard developed by the
International Automotive Task Force for the
automotive industry, focusing on continuous
improvement, defect prevention, and the reduction of
variation and waste in the supply chain
“IC” integratedcircuit,asmallunitorpackagewhichismade
as a single indivisible structure such as a chip and is
electrically equivalent to a conventional circuit of many
separate components
“inch” a unit of length in the imperial system, equal to 2.54
centimeters
“IoT” internet of things, a network of interconnected devices
that collect and exchange data
“ISO14001” an international standard published by the
InternationalOrganizationforStandardization(“ISO”)
that specifies requirements for an effective
environmental management system

GLOSSARY OF TECHNICAL TERMS
“ISO45001” an international standard published by ISO specifying
requirements for an occupational health and safety
management system
“ISO9001” an international standard published by ISO specifying
requirements for a quality management system
“LCD” liquid crystal display, a panel display technology using
liquid crystals modulated by electric fields
“Logic IC” integrated circuits designed to perform logical
operations and control functions
“mature process technologies” semiconductor manufacturing methods based on
well-established, older technology nodes that offer high
yield, stability, and cost efficiency rather than
leading-edge performance
“MCU” microcontroller unit, a small computer on a single
integrated circuit containing a processor core, memory,
and programmable input/output peripherals
“Micro OLED” a type of display technology that integrates organic
light-emitting diodes onto a silicon substrate, enabling
high-resolution, compact and energy-efficient displays
“multi-rail voltage regulation” a power management technique that provides multiple
independent voltage outputs (rails) from a single power
sourcetomeetthediversepowerrequirementsof system
components such as processors, memory, and I/O
interfaces
“nm” nanometer
“OLED” organic light emitting diode, a display technology that
generates light directly from organic materials,
providing superior image quality, energy efficiency and
design flexibility compared to traditional display
technologies
“OSAT” outsourced semiconductor assembly and test,
third-partyserviceprovidersthathandlesemiconductor
packaging and testing
“PDKs” process design kits, collections of files and models used
to design and simulate semiconductor devices for a
specific process
“photomask” a tool used in photolithography to define circuit
patterns on a wafer
“photoresist” a light-sensitive material used to form patterns during
photolithography
“PMIC” power management integrated circuits

=== PAGE 41 ===
GLOSSARY OF TECHNICAL TERMS
“pure-play foundry” aspecializedsemiconductorcompanythatfocusessolely
on the contract manufacturing of wafers for integrated
circuits designed by external clients
“QC080000” acertificationstandardforhazardoussubstanceprocess
management in electronic products
“RF chip” a radio frequency chip, used to enable wireless
communication by transmitting and receiving radio
signals, which is widely applied in mobile devices,
wireless networks and IoT products to support reliable
and efficient connectivity across various applications
“standard cell” a logic circuit block for building ICs
“System on Chip (“SOC”)” an integrated circuit that consolidates multiple
electronic components, such as CPU, GPU, memory,
and I/O controllers, onto a single chip to reduce size,
power consumption and cost while enhancing
performance
“technology nodes” specific generations of semiconductor manufacturing
defined by the size of key features on a chip (measured
in nanometers), representing process scaling and
performance improvements
“thermal oxidation” a process that grows an oxide layer on a silicon wafer by
exposing it to high-temperature oxygen
“transistor” a semiconductor device used to amplify or switch
electronic signals
“wafer” a thin slice of semiconductor material, used in the
manufacture of ICs and other microelectronic devices
“wafer starts” the number of wafers initiated into the fabrication
process, used to measure production capacity
“yield rate” the percentage of functional devices produced from a
batch of wafers
“μm” micrometer, a unit of length equal to one millionth of a
meter (10-6 m)

RISKS RELATING TO OUR BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY
Ourindustryischaracterizedbyrapidtechnologicalchangeandevolvingmarketdemands.If we
are unable to timely implement new manufacturing technologies, keep pace with industry
advancementsoradapttorapidmarketchanges,ourabilitytoretainexistingcustomers,attract
new customers or maintain our market competitiveness may be adversely affected.
The semiconductor foundry industry is characterized by rapid technological evolution,
short product lifecycles and increasingly complex customer requirements. As a pure-play
12-inch wafer foundry, our competitiveness depends on timely adoption and implementation
of manufacturing technologies, such as new technology nodes, device architectures and
integration techniques, and on our ability to respond quickly to changes in customer design
specifications, performance expectations and application-specific requirements across
consumerelectronics,automotiveelectronics,smarthome,industrialcontrol,AI,theIoTand
memory.
Any delays of commercializing our technology platforms in terms of development,
validation or ramp-up, or failure to meet customer performance or yield expectations, could
result in loss of existing business and reduced new customer wins. Rapid shifts in industry
preferences, such as accelerated migration to high-performance nodes or architectural
changes, may reduce demand for mature-node platforms and adversely affect capacity
utilization and pricing; if we cannot align our technology roadmap with industry trends and
customer pipelines or maintain high yields and quality through precise process control and
continuous optimisation, our reputation, market share, pricing power, revenue visibility,
profitability and growth may be materially and adversely affected.
The industry in which we operate is highly competitive. If we fail to compete effectively against
other market players, our business, financial condition and results of operations may be
adversely affected.
Moreover, the wafer foundry industry is marked by high concentration and intense
competition,andsuchcompetitionisexpectedtointensify.AccordingtoFrost&Sullivan,the
toptenglobalwaferfoundriesheldasignificantmarketshareof 96.9%intermsof revenuein
2025.Theintroductionorsignificantadvancementsof newtechnologynodes,bycompetitors,
or our failure to timely develop and commercialize enhanced technology platforms, or
alternative semiconductor technologies platforms, could result in reduced competitiveness.
Some of our competitors may have greater resources, technological and production
capabilities, longer operating history, more extensive IP portfolios, broader sales and
marketing networks and stronger customer relationships. Periods of capacity expansion
across the industry may also lead to oversupply, which could increase price competition,
reduce average selling prices and compress margins, particularly for mature-node platforms.
Customerconsolidationandtheincreasingbargainingpowerof leadingICdesigncompanies
may further intensify pricing pressure and limit our ability to negotiate favorable commercial
terms. If we are unable to maintain our competitive edge, we may experience declines in
market share and profitability, which would adversely affect our business, financial condition
and results of operations.

GLOBAL WAFER FOUNDRY MARKET
Overview
IntegratedCircuit(“IC”),alsoknownasmicrocircuit,microchiporchip,isaminiature
electronic device or component. Through specific production processes, IC manufacturers
interconnects transistors, resistors, capacitors, inductors and other elements required for a
circuit,alongwithwiring,ontowafersubstrates.Thesearethenencapsulatedwithinashellto
form a miniature structure with the desired circuit functions.
The IC production chain involves a number of stages including design, manufacturing,
back-end processes (packaging and testing) and sales. Based on the number of stages that a
company engages in, IC manufacturers can be categorized into three models: the Integrated
Device Manufacturer (“IDM”) model, the Foundry model focused solely on wafer
manufacturing and the Fabless model specialized in chip design and sales. However, as
technological complexity and production costs increase, the IDM model has faced challenges
such as high operational costs and limited production flexibility. In recent years, many IDM
companies have gradually shifted toward a Fabless + Foundry model to reduce production
costs and improve efficiency.

The Size of Global Integrated Circuit Market
The global IC market has grown from US$463.0 billion in 2021 to US$677.9 billion in
2025, representing a CAGR of 10.0%. From the perspective of supply and demand dynamics,
amid the global public health crisis between 2021 and 2022, demand for remote and online
work had surged, driving robust sales of consumer electronics. However, public health
incidents impacting employees’ health and attendance led to lower operating rates at some
wafer foundries and the insufficient production and supply capacity led to a shortage in IC
– 71 –

=== PAGE 81 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
supply, causing IC supply chain tensions and significant increases in IC product prices.
Therefore, the scale of the IC industry reached a phased peak of US$474.4 billion in 2022.
Entering2023,asproductionresumedandsupplychaintensiongraduallyeased,theglobalIC
market size saw a light decrease and the chip prices as well as market demand returned to a
normal level. From 2026 to 2030, the global IC market is expected to expand at a CAGR of
11.2%,reachingUS$1,115.0billionby2030.Drivenbydomesticsubstitutionof ICsandrapid
growth in new downstream applications, the growth rate of the IC market in Chinese
Mainland has consistently outperformed that of the global market, and increased from
US$148.5billionin2021toUS$246.4billionin2025,withaCAGRof 13.5%,andisexpected
toreachUS$474.4billionin2030,representingaCAGRof approximately14.0%from2026to
2030.

According to wafer capacity, the global wafer capacity grew from 28.1 million

with a CAGR of 9.7%.
Fromaglobalperspective,acertainlevelof capacitybuffer—generallyintherangeof
approximately 10% to 20% — is considered normal and necessary in the wafer foundry
industry. Such buffer capacity helps mitigate operational risks arising from unplanned
equipment downtime, natural disasters, supply chain disruptions and geopolitical
uncertainties. Accordingly, this level of capacity buffer does not represent structural
over-capacity.
With respect to the Chinese Mainland market, demand for mature-node wafer foundry
servicescontinuestobesupportedbytherapidgrowthof downstreamapplications,including
consumer electronics, automotive electronics and power management and control ICs related
to artificial intelligence data centers. Given the expanding IC content and long-term demand
drivers in these applications, the Group believes that there is no apparent risk of material
over-capacity for mature-node IC products in the Chinese Mainland market during the
relevant period.

Global Wafer Foundry Market Drivers
Therapidexpansionof diverseapplicationscenarios—includingconsumerelectronics,
automotive electronics, generative AI and robotics — is driving continuous advancements in
chip functionality. These functional improvements contribute to increased value per chip,
whilegrowingdemandensureseconomiesof scalethroughmassproduction.Thecombination
of these factors allows wafer foundries to achieve both higher averages in selling prices and
steady growth in shipment volume, providing a dual boost to the wafer foundry business.
Consumer Electronics
As a critical interface bridging virtual and physical worlds, smart wearable devices are
undergoing rapid evolution. The adoption of head-mounted displays (“HMD”s) and smart
glasses is propelling innovations in DDICs targeting higher refresh rates, lower latency and
refined power control to ensure immersive visual experiences. Meanwhile, the expansion of
spatialawareness,gesturerecognitionandenvironmentalinteractioncapabilitiesisdeepening
the integration of CIS, where miniaturization, high resolution and low power consumption
are emerging as central development thrusts.
Automotive Electronics
Driven by electrification and intelligence, automotive systems increasingly adopt
PMICs, MCUs, Logic ICs and CIS. MCUs enable real-time control and system management
in subsystems such as e-drive and power distribution, facing rising requirements for
deterministic timing and functional safety. Logic ICs support autonomous driving domain
controllers and in-vehicle infotainment with high computing performance, low latency and
multi-sensor fusion capabilities.
Artificial Intelligence
The rapid development of generative AI is primarily characterized by ever-increasing
modelparameters,morefrequenttrainingandinferencecycles,asignificantriseinconcurrent
online service requests and stricter latency targets. These factors collectively demand greater
computingpower,drivingserver-sideconfigurationandarchitecturalupgrades.Ononehand,
the capabilities of Logic ICs in high-performance computing, low-latency processing and
high-bandwidth interconnection serve as a core driver, prompting continuous innovation at
the processing and interconnect levels. On the other hand, high power density and significant
load fluctuations impose stricter requirements on power delivery systems, where PMICs are
– 75 –

=== PAGE 85 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
advancing in conversion efficiency, transient response and stable power delivery to underpin
overall energy efficiency and reliability.
Robot Applications
As robots evolve toward multi-scenario and multi-role applications, core chip
requirementsareupgradingaccordingly.MCUsaremovingtowardhigherdeterminism,lower
power consumption and enhanced reliability for motion control and safety monitoring; edge
Logic ICs are strengthening computing power and low-latency processing to support local
inferenceanddatafusion;andCISapplicationsaredeepeninginperceptiontasks,withhigher
resolution, WDR and improved low-light performance becoming key trends.
Mature Nodes in Stability-Critical Applications
Mature nodes remain the only practical choice in certain stability-critical applications.
In automotive, industrial control, energy management and sensor-related scenarios, the
ability of a chip to operate reliably under varying conditions is more important than
advancing the process node itself. Many controllers, power-related components and sensing
devices rely on the proven consistency, environmental tolerance and predictable performance
of mature processes, attributes that are often difficult or uneconomical to achieve using
advanced nodes. Given the long certification cycles, stringent qualification requirements and
high replacement risks associated with these applications, mature nodes maintain a highly
irreplaceable position and form a stable source of long-term demand.
Automotive-grade ICs are required to operate reliably under harsh conditions,
including high temperatures, high voltages, electrical noise and exposure to dust and
vibration.Matureprocesstechnologiesarebettersuitedtosuchenvironments,astheysupport
high-voltage device structures, offer wider operating temperature ranges and demonstrate
well-validated reliability performance over long service lifecycles.
Manageable Development Costs of Mature Process Platforms
Mature process platforms offer more predictable development and production costs.
With well-established design and verification flows, they enable faster product development,
smoother mass production and lower overall risk. For many peripheral components that
prioritize cost efficiency and operational stability over extreme performance, mature nodes
therefore remain a practical and economically efficient choice.
Development Trends of the Wafer Foundry Market in Chinese Mainland
Demand for Mature Process Technologies Driven by System-Level Design Paradigm Shifts
As system-level chip design paradigms continue to evolve, the role of mature process
nodes within the broader semiconductor architecture is being redefined. System-level design
paradigm shifts refer to a change in semiconductor design philosophy, under which chips are
no longer designed solely to maximize transistor density on a single advanced process node.
Instead, modern semiconductor systems are designed at the system level to balance
performance, reliability, power efficiency, cost and long-term stability across different
functional modules.
Localized Substitution
Against the backdrop of increasing global supply chain instability, the localization of
chip production in China aims to build a self-sufficient, controllable, secure and reliable
supply chain. The self-sufficiency rate of China’s domestic chip industry has been gradually
rising.In2020,theself-sufficiencyrateof China’schipindustrywasonly16.6%.By2025,this
rateincreasedto30.0%.Withthedevelopmentof theentirechipindustrychainandthesteady
progressof importsubstitution,itisprojectedthatChina’schipself-sufficiencyratewillreach
50.0% by 2030.

Balanced Supply-Demand Relationships
With the continuous expansion of market demand, it is expected that downstream
application sectors — including consumer electronics, automotive electronics, generative AI
and robotics — will see sustained growth in their demand for mature-node chips.
Development in these downstream applications drives greater system-level complexity,
expanding the semiconductor content per device. AI-enabled platforms and intelligent
vehicles,forinstance,requireanincreasingarrayof supportingICs—suchasPMICs,MCUs
and DDICs — predominantly produced on mature nodes. This trend underscores the
enduring importance of mature-node technologies, as advanced devices demand broader
functional diversity and deeper integration to ensure stability, reliability and cost efficiency.
This will effectively absorb the newly added production capacity, helping to maintain a
relatively balanced and healthy overall supply and demand in the market. Our diversified
technology platforms enable us to effectively address evolving demand across a wide array of
applications, including consumer electronics, automotive electronics, smart home, industrial
control, AI, the IoT and memory.

CircuitIndustryandtheSoftwareIndustryintheNewEra《( 新時期促進集成電路產業和軟件
產業高質量發展的若干政策》), emphasizing on strengthening supply chain security and
building a complete, sustainable semiconductor ecosystem through fiscal and tax incentives,
support for technological innovation, talent development and the promotion of stable
manufacturing capabilities across different technology nodes. These policies recognize the
strategic importance of mature technologies in enabling critical downstream applications
such as automotive electronics, industrial control and consumer electronics. Such supportive
operating environments effectively guide enterprises to dynamically adjust their investment
pace according to market demand, avoiding disorderly competition and resource wastage.
THE GLOBAL DDIC FOUNDRY MARKET
Definition and Classification of DDIC Foundry
DDICs generally refer to driver integrated circuits with the function of driving the
display of screens. They typically utilize industry-standard universal serial or parallel
interfaces to receive commands and data, and generate signals with appropriate voltage,
current, timing and demultiplexing to enable screens to display the desired text or images.

THE GLOBAL CIS FOUNDRY MARKET
Definition and Classification of CIS Foundry
Imagesensorisanelectroniccomponentthatutilizesarraysof photosensitiveunitsand
auxiliarycontrolcircuitstocapturebrightnessandcolorsignalsfromobjectsandscenes,and
output digital image information through complex signal processing and image processing
technologies. Photodiodes are typically used in the photosensitive units of the image sensors
to achieve the conversion of photoelectric signals. When exposed to light, photodiodes
generate electrical signals with the intensity to be directly proportional to that of the light.

THE GLOBAL LOGIC IC FOUNDRY MARKET
Logic IC is an integrated circuit that contains logical relationships and realizes
calculationandlogicjudgmentfunctionbasedonbinaryprinciple.Itsfunctionscover,among
others, arithmetic and logic operation, timing control, data storage and transmission,
interface protocol processing and error verification, which are widely used in computers,
communication equipment, consumer electronics, artificial intelligence, autonomous driving
and industrial control systems.
With the rapid recovery of the global economy, the global Logic IC foundry market

THE GLOBAL MCU FOUNDRY MARKET
Micro Control Unit (“MCU”) is a microprocessor chip designed for specific
application-oriented control and processing, also known as a single-chip microcomputer. By
integrating key computer components including the CPU, RAM, ROM, timers and various
I/O interfaces into a single chip, it forms a chip-level computer capable of handling data and
operationsfrommultiplesources.Whileitsinstructionexecutionspeedisgenerallylowerthan
that of a dedicated Digital Signal Processor (“DSP”), MCUs are widely used in consumer
devices, automotive systems and industrial applications.

CHALLENGES OF WAFER FOUNDRY
Intensified Competition
In China’s wafer foundry market for DDIC, CIS, PMIC, Logic IC and MCU products,
capacity expansion has accelerated in recent years. More new fabs have entered production,
and additional lines are releasing capacity. As a result, competition has become significantly
moreintense.Undertheseconditions,waferpricesareunlikelytocontinuethestrongupward
trend seen in the past. Any observed price adjustments are primarily driven by cyclical
supply-demanddynamics,includingfluctuationsindownstreamdemand,inventorylevelsand
the timing of capacity additions, rather than reflecting a long-term structural change in the
wafer foundry industry.
Capacity Ramp-Up
AlthoughDDIC,CIS,PMIC,LogicICandMCUproductsusedifferentprocessnodes,
manufacturing them relies heavily on accumulated process experience, stable production
capability and continuous equipment tuning. As Chinese foundries accelerate capacity
expansion across several nodes, many new fabs face similar challenges during their early
stages. These include a longer capacity ramp-up period, slower yield improvement due to
limited familiarity with specific processes and repeated tuning needs for process stability.
In addition, customers in automotive, consumer electronics and industrial applications
usually require long and strict qualification cycles. This extends the time for new fabs or new
processes to be adopted into customer supply chains and puts short-term pressure on
profitability and operating efficiency. Over time, some foundries may gradually improve their
process stability and equipment tuning capabilities.
ANALYSIS OF AND FORECAST FOR KEY RAW MATERIAL COSTS AND MAIN
PRODUCT PRICES
In recent years, the overall price trend of key raw materials for wafer foundry has
exhibited a pattern of “initial surge followed by period stabilization”. In 2021 and 2022,
driven by the rapid release of downstream demand and heightened supply chain tensions, the
pricesof majorinputssuchassiliconwafers,processgasesandphotoresistsrosesignificantly.
Entering 2023 and 2024, with raw materials’ capacity expansion and supply recovery, raw
materialpricesgraduallyreturnedtonormallevel.Lookingahead,asmature-nodecapacities
continue to expand and supply-side pressures ease, we expect overall raw material prices to
show a mild downward trajectory and remain within a relatively reasonable and stable range
over the medium to long term.
Photomasks exhibited a sustained upward price trend due to their high technical
barriers and high industry concentration. As process complexity and precision requirements
increase, the cost proportion of high-end photomasks will continue to rise, becoming a
long-term pressure point in the cost structure of wafer foundry operations.

ANALYSIS OF MARKET COMPETITION
The Competitive Landscape of the Wafer Foundry Industry
Theglobalwaferfoundrymarketdemonstrateshighconcentration,withmanufacturers
inTaiwan,Chinalongdominatingthesectorandestablishingadvantagesinadvancedprocess
technologies.However,manufacturersinChineseMainlandarerapidlyexpandingcapacityin
mature process segments, securing multiple positions among the world’s top ten foundries.
Leveraging local customer demand and accelerated technological iteration, they are
progressively narrowing the gap. Overall, advanced processes remain highly concentrated,
while mature processes are showing the trend of regional diversification. In terms of wafer
foundry revenue in 2025, our Company ranked as the ninth largest wafer foundry globally,
with a market share of 0.9%, and the third largest wafer foundry in Chinese Mainland with a
marketshareof 8.7%.Duringtheperiodfrom2020to2025,ourCompanyachievedthefastest
growth in both production capacity and revenue among the world’s top ten wafer foundries.

ANALYSIS OF INDUSTRY BARRIERS
Technical Barriers. Technical barriers in the wafer foundry market are reflected in the
difficultyinresearchinganddevelopingadvancedprocesses.Asthenodesof processesshrink,
the requirements for precision and materials are gradually increasing, and the R&D costs are
increasing exponentially. High-end equipment is monopolized by a small number of
international enterprises, and the manufacturing of core equipment involves cutting-edge
technologies across multiple fields and is subject to export restrictions.
Equipment and Material Barriers. Wafer foundries rely on a variety of high-end
equipment,suchaslithographymachinesandetchingmachines,whichhashightechnological
complexity, and the market is mainly monopolized by foreign enterprises. For example, in
2020, the proportion of domestic replacement of lithography machines was less than 1%. A
lithographymachinecontains100,000componentparts.Domesticenterprisesstillfallbehind
the international advanced level.
Customer Barriers. There are significant customer barriers for the wafer foundry
market globally and in Chinese Mainland. From a global perspective, the head foundry
enterprises and downstream customers have a close tie-up for a long time, and maintain deep
cooperationthroughjointR&Dandguaranteedpriorityinproductioncapacity,whichmakes
it difficult for new entrants to break through the existing cooperation system.
Talent Barriers. Wafer foundries need a large number of professionals who master
advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies and processes, including engineers and
technicians.Talentcultivationrequiresalongperiodof timeandalotof practicalexperience.
The global competition for semiconductor talents is fierce, and it is difficult for new
enterprises to set up high-caliber talent teams in a short period of time. However, existing
enterprises have attracted and retained a large number of talents through a good working
environment and remuneration, which further raises the entry threshold of the industry.

REGULATIONS ON PRODUCT QUALITY
On December 29, 2018, the SCNPC amended the Product Quality Law of the People’s
Republicof China《( 中華人民共和國產品質量法》)promulgatedonFebruary22,1993,stating
that producers and sellers shall establish a sound internal product quality management
system, strictly adhere to a job responsibility system in relation to quality standards and
quality liabilities, and implement corresponding assessment methods. The Product Quality
Law prohibits the counterfeiting or unauthorized use of quality marks such as certification
marks; prohibits the counterfeiting of a product’s place of origin, or the counterfeiting or
unauthorized use of another factory’s name or address; prohibits mixing impurities or fakes
into products during production or sales, passing off fake products as genuine, or passing off
substandard products as standard.
REGULATIONS ON THE IC INDUSTRY
In June 2014, the State Council promulgated the Outline for Promoting the
Development of the National Integrated Circuit Industry《( 國家集成電路產業發展推進綱要》),
which stated that the development goal of the integrated circuit industry is to reach an
advancedinternationalstandardinthemajorlinksof theintegratedcircuitindustrychainby
2030, with a number of enterprises entering the international first tier and achieving leapfrog
development. One of the main tasks and development priorities are to focus on the
development of integrated circuit design industry when strengthening collaborative
innovation in integrated circuit design, software development, system integration, content
and services based on the industrial chain in key areas so as to drive the manufacturing
industry developing with the rapid growth of the design industry.
In July 2020, the State Council announced Several Policies for Promoting High-quality
Development of the Integrated Circuit Industry and the Software Industry in the New Era
(《新時期促進集成電路產業和軟件產業高質量發展的若干政策》), in order to further optimize
the development environment of the integrated circuit industry and software sectors, deepen
international cooperation in the industry, and enhance the industrial innovation capability
and development quality, launch a series of supporting fiscal and taxation, investment and
financing, research and development, import and export, talents, intellectual property rights,
market application and international cooperation policies.

a foreign investor, individually or collectively with other investors, establishes the

inthecaseof aninvention,tenyearsinthecaseof utilitymodelsandfifteenyearsinthecase

Copyrights
Pursuant to the Copyright Law of the People’s Republic of China《( 中華人民共和國著
作權法》) (the “Copyright Law”) promulgated by the State Council on September 7, 1990 and
amended in 2001, 2010 and 2020 and Regulations for Implementation of Copyright Law of
the People’s Republic of China《( 中華人民共和國著作權法實施條例》) published on May 30,
1991 and amended in 2002, 2011 and 2013, Chinese citizens, legal persons or unincorporated
organizations shall, whether published or not, enjoy copyright in their works. The copyrights
include personal rights such as the right of publication and that of attribution as well as
property rights such as the right of reproduction and that of distribution. The scope of
copyright protection was extended to internet activities, products disseminated over the

distributing,performing,projecting,broadcastingorcompilingaworkorcommunicatingthe
same to the public via an information network without permission from the owner of the

and implemented on March 1, 2013, computer software to be protected under such
Regulations must be independently developed by developers and has been fixed on certain

Pursuant to the Measures for the Registration of Computer Software Copyright

Trademark Rights
According to the Trademark Law of the People’s Republic of China《( 中華人民共和國
商標法》), which was promulgated by the SCNPC on August 23, 1982, last amended on April
23, 2019 with effect from November 1, 2019, as well as the Implementation Regulation of the
People’sRepublicof ChinaTrademarkLaw《( 中華人民共和國商標法實施條例》)promulgated
by the State Council on August 3, 2002, amended on April 29, 2014 and taking effect from
May 1, 2014, the term of validity of a registered trademark shall be ten years, and may be
renewed for successive ten-year periods upon expiration if the trademark is to remain in use.
The trademark registration in the PRC follows a first-come principle. Applying for the
registration of a trademark may not prejudice the existing right first obtained by others, nor
may any person register in advance a trademark that has already been used by another party
and has already gained a sufficient degree of reputation through such party’s use. Using a
trademark that is identical with or similar to a registered trademark in connection with the
same or similar goods without the authorization of the owner of the registered trademark
constitutes an infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark.

管理辦法》)promulgatedbytheMIITonAugust24,2017andcameintoeffectonNovember1,
2017, the MIIT shall be responsible for managing internet domain name in the PRC. The
first-come principle is implemented for domain name registration services where the
corresponding detailed rules for domain name registration stipulate otherwise, such
provisions shall prevail. Domain name registrations are handled through domain name
serviceagenciesestablishedundertherelevantregulations,andtheapplicantsbecomedomain
name holders upon successful registration.

sensitive industries shall be subject to administration of verification and approval by the
NDRC, and non-sensitive outbound investment projects shall be subject to administration by
record-filing.
REGULATIONS ON IMPORT AND EXPORT
AccordingtotheForeignTradeLawof thePeople’sRepublicof China《( 中華人民共和

According to the Customs Law of the People’s Republic of China《( 中華人民共和國海

all its aspects, including supervising the transportation vehicles, goods, luggage, postal
articles and other articles entering and leaving the country, collecting customs duties and
other taxes and fees, preventing and combating smuggling, compiling customs statistics and
handling other customs operations.
In addition, according to the Regulations of the People’s Republic of China on

import and export goods and customs declaration enterprises that have been officially filed
with the customs. If the enterprises apply for filing, they shall obtain the qualification of
market entities. The filing of the customs declaration entities is valid for long term.
REGULATIONS ON TAXATION
Enterprise Income Tax
The NPC promulgated the EIT Law on March 16, 2007 and revised it on February 24,
2017andDecember29,2018.TheImplementationRegulationsof EnterpriseIncomeTaxLaw
of the People’s Republic of China 《( 中華人民共和國企業所得稅法實施條例》) was
promulgated by the State Council on December 6, 2007, took effect on January 1, 2008, and
was revised twice on April 23, 2019 and December 6, 2024. According to the EIT Law and its
implementationregulations,“residententerprises”areenterpriseswhicharesetupinChinain
accordance with law, or which are set up in accordance with the law of a foreign country
(region) but which are actually under the administration of institutions in China. Resident
enterprises shall pay enterprise income tax on their income derived from both within and
outside China; “non-resident enterprises”are enterprises which are set up in accordance with
the law of a foreign country (region) and whose actual administrative institution is not in
China, but which have institutions or establishments in China, or which have no such
institutions or establishments but have income generated from inside China. The rate of
enterprise income tax shall be 25%, however, a non-resident enterprise is generally subject to
a 20% corporate income tax on PRC-sourced income, if it does not have an establishment or

Value-added tax
According to the Provisional Regulations on Value-added Tax of the People’s Republic

Pursuant to the Guidelines on Tax Preference Policies for Software and Integrated

production, packaging and testing, equipment, and material enterprises enjoy an additional
deductionof 15%of theinputVATthatcanbecreditedinthecurrentperiodfromtheoutput
VAT payable. A list management system will be adopted for enterprises eligible for the
additional deduction policy.

REGULATIONS ON ANTI-MONOPOLY AND ANTI-UNFAIR COMPETITION
PursuanttotheAnti-MonopolyLawof thePeople’sRepublicof China《( 中華人民共和
國反壟斷法》) (the “Anti-Monopoly Law”) promulgated by the SCNPC on August 30, 2007,
which came into effect on August 1, 2008 and last amended on June 24, 2022, the prohibited
monopolisticactsincludemonopolisticagreements,abuseof adominantmarketpositionand
concentration of businesses that may have the effect to eliminate or restrict competition.
According to the provisions of the Anti-Monopoly Law, “monopolistic agreements”refer to
the agreements, decisions or other concerted practices to eliminate or restrict competition.
Competing business operators, or operators and their transaction counterparties, are
prohibited to enter into monopoly agreements specified by the Anti-Monopoly Law between
each other, unless the agreement will satisfy the exemptions under the Anti-Monopoly Law.
“Abuse of dominant market position” refers to a business operator with a dominant market
position to abuse its dominant market position to conduct acts, including seven prohibited
categories of acts listed in the Anti-Monopoly Law, among others: (1) selling commodities at
unfairlyhighpricesorbuyingcommoditiesatunfairlylowprices;(2)sellingproductsatprices
belowcostwithoutanyjustifiablecause;(3)refusingtotradewithatradingpartywithoutany
justifiable cause. “Concentration of undertakings” refers to (1) merger of undertakings; (2)
acquisition of control over other undertakings by an undertaking through acquisition of
equityorassets;(3)acquisitionof controloverotherundertakingsbyanundertakingthrough
contract or any other means or ability to exert decisive impact on other undertakings.
Pursuant to the provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People’s
Republic of China《( 中華人民共和國反不正當競爭法》) (the “Anti-Unfair Competition Law”)
promulgatedbytheSCNPConSeptember2,1993,latestamendedonJune27,2025andcame
into effect on the same day, “unfair competition” refers to that the operator disrupts the
market competition order and damages the legitimate rights and interests of other operators
or consumers in violation of the provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law in the
production and operating activities. Pursuant to the provisions of the Anti-Unfair
Competition Law, operators: (1) shall not conduct misleading behaviors; (2) shall not bribe
the entities or individuals with property or by other means; (3) shall neither not conduct any
false or misleading commercial publicity in respect of the performance, functions, quality,
sales, user reviews, and honors received of its commodities to defraud or mislead consumers,
nor help other operators to conduct false or misleading commercial publicity by means
including organizing false transactions; (4) shall not infringe on trade secrets; (5) shall not
fabricateordisseminatefalseormisleadinginformationordamagethebusinessreputationof
the competitors or their goods. Furthermore, operators conducting sales with prizes or
engaging in production or operations activities online shall also abide by the relevant
provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

REGULATIONS ON SECURITIES AND FILING FOR OVERSEAS LISTING
Laws and Regulations on Securities
ThePRCSecuritiesLaw,whichwaspromulgatedbytheSCNPConDecember29,1998,
and was latest amended on December 28, 2019 and took effect on March 1, 2020,
comprehensively regulates the trading activities in the Chinese Mainland securities market
including issuance and trading of securities, takeovers of listed companies, the duties and
responsibilities of securities exchanges, securities companies and securities regulatory
authorities, etc. The PRC Securities Law further regulates that a domestic enterprise issuing
securities overseas directly or indirectly or listing their securities overseas for trading shall
comply with the relevant provisions of the State Council. The CSRC is the securities
regulatory body set up by the State Council to supervise the securities market according to
law,maintainorderinthemarket.Currently,theissueandtradingof Hsharesareprincipally
governed by the laws and regulations, rules and normative documents promulgated by the
State Council and the CSRC.
Filing for Overseas Listings
Pursuant to the Overseas Listing Trial Measures《( 境外上市試行辦法》) released by the
CSRC on February 17, 2023 and became effective on March 31, 2023, together with
supporting guidelines applicable for regulation rules, the unified management of filings shall
be implemented for direct or indirect overseas offerings of securities and listings by domestic
enterprises. All issuers are required to complete the filing procedures and report relevant
information to the security regulatory authority of the State Council. Issuers listing directly
in overseas markets are required to file with the CSRC within three working days after
submitting its application for overseas listing. Pursuant to the provisions of the Overseas
Listing Trial Measures, no overseas offering of securities and listing shall be made under any
of the following circumstances for domestic enterprises:
(1) such financing for listing is explicitly prohibited by provisions in laws,
administrative regulations or relevant state rules;
(2) the overseas securities offering and listing may endanger national security as
reviewed and determined by relevant competent authorities under the State
Council in accordance with law;
(3) thedomesticenterprise,itscontrollingshareholdersortheactualcontroller,have
committed criminal offenses such as corruption, bribery, misappropriation of
property, embezzlement, or undermining the order of the socialist market
economy during the recent three years;
(4) the domestic enterprise is suspected of committing criminal offenses or major
violations of laws, and is under investigation according to law and no conclusion
or opinion has yet been made thereof;
(5) there are material ownership disputes over equity held by its controlling
shareholders or by shareholders that are controlled by the controlling
shareholder or actual controller.
Pursuant to the Provisions on Strengthening the Confidentiality and Archives
Administration Related to the Overseas Securities Offering and Listing by Domestic
Enterprises《( 關於加強境內企業境外發行證券和上市相關保密和檔案管理工作的規定》), when
domestic enterprises issue and list securities on overseas markets, they shall establish
confidentiality and archives management systems.

REGULATIONS ON ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION
According to the Environmental Protection Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國環境保
護法》), as revised by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on April 24,
2014 and implemented on January 1, 2015, enterprises, institutions and other producers or
operators that discharge pollutants are required to take measures to prevent and control
pollution and harm to the environment caused by waste gas, wastewater, waste residue,
medical waste, dust, malodorous gases, radioactive substances, as well as noise, vibration,
light radiation and electromagnetic radiation generated during production, construction or
other activities.
Pursuant to the Environmental Impact Assessment Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國
環境影響評價法》),promulgatedandimplementedbytheStandingCommitteeof theNational
People’s Congress on December 29, 2018, the Regulations on the Administration of
Environmental Protection for Construction Projects《( 建設項目環境保護管理條例》), revised
by the State Council on July 16, 2017 and implemented on October 1, 2017, and the Interim
Measures for the Acceptance of Environmental Protection Facilities upon Completion of
Construction Projects, promulgated and implemented by the former Ministry of
Environmental Protection on November 20, 2017, an environmental impact assessment
system is implemented for construction projects within China. Construction entities must
submit an environmental impact report or environmental impact form for approval prior to
commencement of construction, or file an environmental impact registration form in
accordance with the requirements of the administrative department for environmental
protection under the State Council.
According to the Law of the PRC on the Prevention and Control of Environmental
Pollution by Solid Waste 《( 中華人民共和國固體廢物污染環境防治法》), as revised by the
StandingCommitteeof theNationalPeople’sCongressonApril29,2020andimplementedon
September 1, 2020, entities and individuals that generate, collect, store, transport, utilize or
dispose of solid waste must take measures to prevent or reduce environmental pollution
caused by solid waste and bear responsibility for any environmental pollution caused in
accordance with the law.
According to the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the PRC《( 中華人民
共和國水污染防治法》), as revised by the Standing Committee of the National People’s
Congress on June 27, 2017 and implemented on January 1, 2018, enterprises, institutions and
other producers or operators that directly or indirectly discharge industrial wastewater,
medical sewage, or other wastewater or sewage for which a discharge permit is required, must
obtain a discharge permit.
U.S. OUTBOUND INVESTMENT RESTRICTIONS
In August 2023, former President Biden issued Executive Order 14105, “Addressing
United States Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in
Countries of Concern”(the “Executive Order”). In accordance with the Executive Order, on
October 28, 2024, the U.S. Department of the Treasury released new regulations (the “Final
Rule”) prohibiting or requiring notification of U.S. outbound investments in certain
Chinese-affiliated companies operating in the semiconductor and microelectronics, quantum
information technology, and artificial intelligence sectors (“covered foreign persons”). The
Final Rule took effect on January 2, 2025. The Final Rule imposes additional diligence
responsibilities, record-keeping, and notification requirements and restrictions on U.S.
persons and their controlled foreign entities.
• Requirements on U.S. persons: The Final Rule imposes investment prohibition
and notification requirements on U.S. Persons for a wide range of investments in
entities associated with China (including Hong Kong and Macau) that are
engaged in activities relating to three sectors: (i) semiconductors and
microelectronics, (ii) quantum information technologies, and (iii) artificial
intelligencesystems,collectivelydefinedas“coveredactivities”.Inaddition,U.S.

persons are required to take all reasonable steps to prohibit and prevent a
controlled foreign entity from engaging in a prohibited transaction; and are
obligatedtofileanotificationwithrespecttoanotifiabletransactionundertaken
by a controlled foreign entity no later than 30 calendar days after the completion
date of the regulated transaction.
• Specific categories of covered transactions: The Final Rule applies to certain
transactions by U.S. persons, including the acquisition of an equity interest or
contingentequityinterest;certaindebtfinancingthataffordscertainrightstothe

As advised by our U.S. Export Control and Sanctions Legal Advisor, considering our

affecting the investor sentiment towards us, and therefore negatively impacting our ability to
raise capital.

HISTORY, DEVELOPMENT AND CORPORATE STRUCTURE
OVERVIEW
Our history can be traced back to May 2015 when our Company was established by
Hefei Construction Investment, at the initiative of the Hefei government and in technical
cooperation with Powerchip Investment Holding Corporation (“PIHC”). Through over a
decade of development, we have become a leading pure-play 12-inch wafer foundry, offering
wafer fabrication services to global customers. Leveraging our proprietary technologies and
R&D capabilities, our technology platforms span across technology nodes from 150nm to
28nm. According to Frost & Sullivan, in 2024, we ranked as the ninth largest wafer foundry
worldwide and the third largest in Chinese Mainland by revenue.
In November 2020, our Company was converted to a joint stock limited company. In
May2023,ourCompanybecamelistedontheSTARMarketof theShanghaiStockExchange
(stock code: 688249).

OVERVIEW
Who We Are
We are a leading pure-play foundry specializing in 12-inch wafer manufacturing,
operating at a critical juncture of the global semiconductor value chain. As dedicated wafer
fabricationserviceproviders,foundriestranslateICdesignblueprintsfromfabless,fabliteand
integrated device manufacturer (“IDM”) companies into high-quality processed wafers at
scale.
Since inception, we have focused on the advancement of process technologies. Our
foundry services cover technology nodes ranging from 150nm to 40nm, with the 28nm Logic
IC platform successfully developed as of the Latest Practicable Date, positioning us to
address evolving demand for higher-performance and more power-efficient semiconductor
solutions. Our process capabilities are centered on key application-specific IC categories,
including display driver ICs (“DDIC”) that enable display control, complementary
metal-oxide-semiconductor image sensors (“CIS”) that enable image sensing, and power
management ICs (“PMIC”) that regulate and optimize power usage. Our Logic ICs, which
support data processing, and microcontroller units (“MCU”), which provide embedded
control, have also scaled rapidly during the Track Record Period. Leveraging this portfolio,
we are able to support a broad spectrum of applications across consumer electronics,
automotiveelectronics,industrialcontrol,artificialintelligence(“AI”),theInternetof Things
(“IoT”) and memory.
Our ability to combine differentiated process technologies with stable manufacturing
scale has strengthened our position in the global foundry landscape. From 2020 to 2025, we
achieved the fastest growth in production capacity and revenue among the global top ten
wafer foundries, according to Frost & Sullivan. In 2025, we ranked as the ninth largest wafer
foundry worldwide and the third largest in Chinese Mainland by revenue, according to the
same source.

Our Business Model
The wafer foundry industry constitutes a critical pillar of the global semiconductor
value chain. Based on upstream supply of essential materials and technologies including
silicon wafers, photoresists, specialty chemicals, core equipment, electronic design
automation(“EDA”)toolsandintellectualproperty(“IP”)licensing,waferfoundriesprovide
specialized wafer fabrication services for IC design companies, including fabless, fablite and
IDMcompanies,manufacturingtheirICdesignblueprintsintoprocessedwaferswithquality
at scale. While fabless companies fully outsource wafer fabrication to wafer foundries, fablite
andIDMcompanieswithin-houseICmanufacturingcapabilitiesmayalsopartnerwithwafer
foundries to access specialized technologies, secure stable production capacity and enhance
cost effectiveness. These processed wafers are further delivered to IC design companies for
packagingandtestingbyOutsourcedSemiconductorAssemblyandTest(“OSAT”)providers,
which are then integrated by IC design companies into end products across a wide range of
applications such as consumer electronics, automotive electronics, industrial control,
artificial intelligence (“AI”), the Internet of Things (“IoT”) and memory.
Within this value chain, we operate as a pure-play 12-inch wafer foundry, bridging
technology development with large-scale manufacturing to deliver power-efficient,
high-performanceICs.Ourtechnologyplatformportfoliooffersfabricationservicesprimarily
including DDIC, CIS and PMIC, with Logic IC and MCU scaling rapidly during the Track
RecordPeriod.WeserveadiversifiedcustomerbasecomprisingleadingICdesigncompanies,
including fabless, fablite and IDM companies, across end markets including consumer
electronics, automotive electronics, smart home, industrial control, AI, the IoT and memory.
In wafer fabrication, silicon wafer sizes have evolved from the initial 6-inch and 8-inch
formatstothecurrentmainstream12-inch.While8-inchproductionlinescontinuetosupport
legacy applications, incremental capacity growth now primarily stems from 12-inch wafers,
which, with a surface area approximately 2.25 times that of 8-inch wafers, offer significantly
higherdieoutputandenhancedcostperwaferatthesameyield.Specializingin12-inchwafer
fabrication, we achieve high integration density, compact component design and superior
electrical performance.
The level of technological sophistication in wafer fabrication services is typically
reflected by process technology nodes. According to Frost & Sullivan, leading-edge nodes at
or below 7nm are used in high-performance processors, AI accelerators, flagship smartphone
system-on-chips (“SOC”) and advanced networking chips to address compute-intensive logic
tasks. Advanced nodes ranging from 10nm to 22nm are typically adopted for applications
requiringbalancedperformanceandintegration,suchasmid-rangeconsumerSOCs,high-end
MCU, CIS and PMIC designs. Downstream applications such as industrial control, the IoT,
display and power devices generally have a sustained and stringent requirement of
semiconductorproductsforlong-termreliabilityandoperationalrobustness,whichunderpins
the continued and widespread adoption of mature nodes at 28nm and above. For critical
componentsincludingDDIC,CIS,PMICsandMCUs,maturenodesarewidelypreferreddue
to their well-established and extensively validated manufacturing processes. Chips fabricated
using such mature node technologies typically feature thicker gate oxide layers, which help
reduce electric field intensity and enhance voltage tolerance. Their relatively longer
conductive channels further contribute to stable electrical performance under variations in
temperature and operating voltage. In addition, mature node platforms often incorporate
dedicated high-voltage device structures designed to effectively distribute electrical stress,
thereby materially improving device reliability over extended operating lifecycles. These
inherent technical attributes make mature nodes a natural choice for safety-critical and
high-voltage applications, sustaining robust market demand. In addition, industry
performance is commonly assessed based on key operational metrics including wafer sales
volume,productioncapacityandyieldrate.Ourcomprehensiveportfolioof waferfabrication
– 104 –

=== PAGE 114 ===
BUSINESS
services cover technology nodes that had positioned us as one of the leaders among domestic
peers across multiple product categories, reaching 40nm for DDIC, 55nm for CIS and Logic
IC and 110nm for PMIC and MCU as of the Latest Practicable Date, according to the same
source.
By integrating process expertise, yield optimization and cost discipline, we provide a

Our business process spans the entire value chain from design enablement to wafer
fabrication, testing, warehousing and delivery. Our business process primarily includes the
following stages:
• Pre-order Communication and Order Confirmation (duration varies based on
customer requirements). In the initial stage, the sales and marketing team works
with customers to confirm requirements, while the R&D team assesses technical
feasibility. Customers may adopt third-party or self-developed IP cores through

vendors and EDA providers where required. Upon alignment of process
specifications,pricinganddeliveryschedule,ordersareconfirmedandscheduled
for production.

and production to drive continuous process improvement.
OUR PRODUCTION CAPABILITIES
Overview
We operate a large-scale, integrated production base specializing in 12-inch wafer

Province. Our production base supports a wide range of product categories with technology
nodes from 150nm to 40nm as of the Latest Practicable Date. As of December 31, 2025, the

Equipped with wafer fabrication equipment, precision metrology systems and intelligent
manufacturing systems, our production base enables seamless resource coordination and
operational synergies across multiple technology platforms.
Our Wafer Fabrication Process
Wafer fabrication involves a series of complex and precisely controlled process steps
that transform raw silicon wafers into fully functional semiconductor chips. Our production
cycle typically ranges from one to 3.5 months, depending on the product type, technology
node and the complexity of the production process. The fabrication process can be grouped
into the following stages:
Thermal
