– 113 –

=== PAGE 123 ===
BUSINESS
• Pre-processing. The process begins with wafer cleaning to remove any surface
contaminants before high-temperature processing. Key materials include acids,
hydrogen peroxide and high-purity deionized water, while major equipment
includes automated wet benches and wafer scrubbers.
• Patterning. Photolithography is the core process for patterning ICs on the wafer,
involvingthreemainsteps:coatingthewaferwithphotoresist,exposingittolight
through a photomask to transfer the circuit pattern and developing the wafer to
reveal the pattern. This step is repeated many times and uses photoresist
chemicals,developers,solventsandultra-flatquartzphotomasks.Keyequipment
includes spin coaters, mask aligners or stepper/scanner systems and automated
developers. We then proceed to etching, where unprotected material is selectively
removedusingvariousmethods.Dryetching,whichincludesplasmaandreactive
ion etching, and wet chemical etching are used selectively depending on the
material layer. These processes employ etching gases such as CF , SF or Cl
4 6 2
mixtures and liquid etchants such as buffered oxide solutions. The steps are
carried out in high-precision plasma etchers and wet process stations equipped
with exhaust and contamination-control systems.
• Functional Layer Formation. Ion implantation introduces specific dopant ions,
suchasboron,phosphorusorarsenic,intodesignatedregionsof thewaferunder
vacuum and low temperature. This step is executed using ion implanter
equipment and high-purity dopant gas sources (including diborane, phosphine
and arsine). We implement high-temperature annealing to repair crystal lattice
damage and adjust the wafer’s electrical properties. Annealing is performed in
rapid thermal processing furnaces or diffusion furnaces at temperatures of
900°C–1,050°C. During diffusion, dopant ions migrate within the wafer at high
temperatures to form regions with distinct electrical characteristics. Chemical
Vapor Deposition (“CVD”) deposits thin, solid films on the wafer surface
through chemical reactions of gaseous precursors, while Physical Vapor
Deposition (“PVD”) uses techniques such as sputtering or evaporation to
physically deposit thin films. CVD typically uses gases such as silane (SiH ),
4
ammonia(NH )ordichlorosilane(SiH Cl ),andisperformedinlow-pressureor
3 2 2
plasma-enhanced CVD reactors. PVD employs metal targets (such as aluminum,
copper, titanium) and uses sputtering or evaporation chambers. Chemical
Mechanical Polishing (“CMP”) combines mechanical and chemical processes to
planarize the wafer surface, ensuring the required flatness for subsequent layers.
CMP involves the use of polishing pads, slurry chemicals (silica- or
alumina-based), and high-precision CMP tools.
• Testing and Storage. Upon completion of wafer processing, electrical and
functional testing is conducted using probe stations and other inspection
equipment to verify compliance with customer specifications. Typical test stages
includeparametrictesting,wafersortanddefectinspection,usingautomatictest
equipment, optical inspection systems and probe cards. Wafers that pass
inspection are vacuum-packed and stored for delivery. Packaging materials
include anti-static carriers and vacuum-sealed bags, and they are then stored in
temperature- and humidity-controlled environments.

Our Technology Platform
We have developed a suite of technology platforms that integrate process technologies,
device architectures and manufacturing capabilities to support the production of diverse IC
products on 12-inch wafers. Our process technologies refer to the semiconductor fabrication
flows we have adapted across different technology nodes. Device architectures encompass the
integration of functional elements such as transistors, memory cells and analog modules,
tailored to end-use requirements.
Our technology platform portfolio primarily supports the fabrication of DDIC, CIS
andPMIC,withLogicICandMCUscalingrapidlyduringtheTrackRecordPeriod.Building
ondiversetechnologynodesspanningfrom150nmto28nm,eachplatformisconfiguredwith
application-specific process modules and a rich set of device options, such as high-voltage
transistors, embedded non-volatile memory and imaging structures, to address the functional
requirements of different end applications and enhance product performance, cost efficiency
and design flexibility. These platforms form the foundation of our foundry services, enabling
us to deliver optimal power performance, enhanced processing speed, integration density and
manufacturability across a broad range of applications.

DDIC
We provide foundry services for a wide range of DDICs used in flat-panel displays for
televisions, smartphones, tablets and other consumer electronics, which remained our largest
revenue contributor, during the Track Record Period. DDICs are essential for controlling the
voltage and timing of pixel activation, and require high-voltage process modules to drive
display pixels effectively. Advanced DDIC products demand high integration density to
accommodatecomplexcontrolfunctionswithinalimitedchiparea,particularlyinmobileand
high-resolution display applications. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we provided wafer
fabrication services for DDICs across mainstream technology nodes from 150nm to 40nm,
supporting a range of display driver applications, with each node tailored to specific end-use
requirements such as high-resolution smartphones, tablets and television displays.
DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,weprimarilyprovidedLCDDDICswhichcontrolthe
alignment of liquid crystals to modulate light from a backlight and produce images. We are
actively advancing the development of DDIC solutions tailored for high-growth verticals.
OLED panels use organic light-emitting diodes to deliver enhanced image quality and energy
efficiency, enabling vibrant colors, ultra-thin design, fast response, wide viewing angles and
flexible display form. Rising demand for OLED panels is set to fuel increased shipments of
OLED DDICs which serve as the core control units for OLED panels. To actively strengthen
our foothold in the OLED DDIC market, we had commenced mass production of 40nm
high-voltage OLED DDICs and were making steady progress in developing our
state-of-the-art 28nm OLED DDIC platform as of the Latest Practicable Date. In addition,
we are also actively advancing silicon-based Micro OLED technologies for AR/VR and the
wearable sector, and automotive-grade DDICs for the automotive electronics. These
developments significantly enhance our ability to serve the increasingly diversified and
specialized display requirements of emerging end markets.

CIS
CIS serves as the core visual components across a wide range of applications including
main cameras for smartphones, automotive camera modules and industrial vision. CIS
products typically require advanced imaging structures, complex pixel architectures and high
levels of analog-digital integration, resulting in stringent process requirements and tight
defect controls.
Leveraging our mature 90nm and 55nm technology platforms, we support mainstream
and high-performance CIS production. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had achieved
mass production of 90nm CIS products, 55nm mid-to-high-end BSI and 55nm full-process
stacked CIS for use in the main cameras of mid- to high-end smartphones, with product
resolutions reaching up to 50 megapixels. In addition, we are steadily advancing the
technological development for 40nm CIS products to support customer demand for
next-generationimagesensorsolutionswithhigherresolutionandimprovedenergyefficiency.
As markets such as smartphones, new energy vehicles, AR/VR and machine vision gain
traction, the CIS market is poised for sustained growth. We are focused on expanding our
presence in the image sensor sector, with the goal of becoming the largest domestic foundry
supplier in the field. Our technology platforms and manufacturing capabilities position us to
capture the significant opportunities arising from the ongoing transformation and expansion
of the CIS market.
PMIC
PMICs are highly integrated semiconductor chips that provide comprehensive power
management solutions for a wide range of electronic systems. They perform essential
functions such as power conversion, voltage regulation, sequencing and monitoring, serving
as the central hub for power supply and distribution within electronic products. PMICs are
indispensablecomponentsthatdirectlyinfluencetheperformance,efficiencyandreliabilityof
modern electronic devices and are widely used across electrical and electronic systems. As of
the Latest Practicable Date, we had achieved mass production of PMIC products on the
150nmand110nmplatform,andwereactivelydeveloping90nmPMICs,furtherextendingour
reach into additional application sectors.
As electronic products become more varied and energy efficiency requirements become
more stringent, PMICs are expected to play an even more critical role in enabling
high-performance, energy-efficient and reliable electronic systems, especially for applications
acrossrapidlygrowingmarketssuchasAI,bigdataandtheIoT.Ourongoinginnovationand
leadership in power management technologies position us to capture the significant
opportunities arising from these industry trends and reinforce our competitive advantage in
the PMIC sector.

applications with robust growth potential, spanning consumer electronics, automotive
electronics, smart home, industrial control, AI, the IoT and memory.
• Logic IC. Our Logic IC on 150nm, 110nm and 55nm technology platforms are

RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
Our R&D capabilities form the cornerstone of our technological advancement and
business growth. Supported by our experienced R&D team, we have established our R&D
capabilities across mainstream technology nodes from 150nm to 40nm, and have completed
the development of 28nm Logic IC platforms. Our R&D initiatives primarily focus on
advancing technology performance, diversifying application platforms and accelerating the
industrialization of new technologies. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest
Practicable Date, we did not have any external parties involved in our R&D activities.
We have consistently made substantial investments in R&D during the Track Record
Period. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our research and development expenses amounted to
RMB1,057.5 million, RMB1,284.0 million and RMB1,453.4 million, respectively. Through
sustained investment and close alignment with customer needs, we have built distinctive
strengthsinmaturetechnologynodesacrossDDIC,CISandPMICplatforms,withourLogic
IC and MCU platforms scaling rapidly during the Track Record Period. Our continual R&D
investment and technical advancements have resulted in a considerable portfolio of
intellectual property, covering key technical areas such as semiconductor device structures,
manufacturing processes, yield optimization, power efficiency and reliability enhancement.
As of December 31, 2025, we held 1,374 patents, including 1,057 invention patents; and had
354 patent applications, including 237 invention patent applications in the PRC and other
jurisdictions.
Our R&D Team
WehaveestablishedastableandhighlyexperiencedR&Dteamthatplaysapivotalrole
indrivingourtechnologyadvancementandplatformdevelopment.Asof December31,2025,
we had 1,976 R&D personnel, accounting for approximately 34.6% of our total employee
headcount, with approximately 69.0% of our R&D personnel holding a master’s degree or
above. As of December 31, 2025, our core R&D team comprises experts with an average of
over ten years of relevant industry experience from both domestic and international
semiconductor companies, and a strong track record in display drivers, image sensors, power
management and Logic IC design and integration. Our R&D efforts focus on developing
technology nodes and related enabling technologies. We build our team through targeted
hiring and structured internal training, supported by a mentorship system that gives junior
engineers practical experience in troubleshooting and process optimization.
Our R&D Mechanism
We have established a comprehensive R&D management system governed by clearly
defined policies and procedures that delineate the roles, responsibilities and workflows of
each department involved in the R&D process. This system enables us to maximize resource
efficiency, maintain rigorous technical standards and focus on long-term platform
development and commercial viability.
Our R&D process comprises four stages: (i) project initiation and feasibility
assessment, where we review market needs and technical viability to determine whether a
projectproceeds;(ii)technicaldevelopment,duringwhichourR&Dteamdevelops,optimizes

global wafer foundry industry, which naturally features a high degree of customer
concentration due to the limited number of leading IC design companies with large
production volumes and stringent qualification requirements for foundry suppliers. Our key
customers are recognized industry leaders in the display driver, image sensor and power
management segments, whose stable demand and long-term purchase arrangements have
contributed significantly to our revenue base. The concentration further reflects long-term
mutual support as customers depend on our technology platforms and stable output while we
maintain close collaboration and consistent supply, sustaining durable partnerships.

We recorded certain fluctuations in the revenue attributable to our largest and five

primarily driven by the cyclical nature of the global semiconductor industry, inventory

dynamics in downstream markets such as consumer electronics. These variations also reflect
the natural progression of our business, including the transition of CIS products into mass
production and the deepening of cooperation with key customers, which led to shifts in order
volumes across different reporting periods.

OUR PROCUREMENT
The production of wafers relies on high-quality raw materials and equipment. During
the Track Record Period, we primarily procured raw materials such as production-grade
silicon wafers, chemicals, gases, sputtering targets, photoresists and components, as well as
equipmentusedinwaferfabrication,mainlyfromEastAsia,Europe,NorthAmerica,Chinese
Mainland and Taiwan, China.
We have established internal mechanisms to maintain stable quality and continuity in
the supply of raw materials and equipment. We only source from suppliers who pass
qualification reviews, efficiency checks and on-site assessments based on technical capability,
product quality, credentials, reputation and pricing. To strengthen supply-chain stability, we
diversify our supplier base and prioritize the integration of domestic suppliers. We also
conduct ongoing evaluations of quality, pricing and service to maintain a closed-loop
procurement management process. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest
Practicable Date, we generally maintained multiple suppliers for key raw materials and
manufacturing equipment to avoid over-reliance on any single source.
To mitigate potential impact from increases in raw material costs, we entered into
long-term agreements with some suppliers of key raw materials. We have also established
flexible pricing mechanism with suppliers in response to the market pricing fluctuations, and
implementedperiodicreviewstomonitorourcostsbytakingintoconsiderationourinventory
levels, sales prospects and market trends. We did not experience any material shortage of
supply, quality issue, disruptions, disputes or delays in relation to the supply from suppliers,
or any material breach of our contractual arrangements with suppliers during the Track
Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date.

our products. We conduct regular process optimization and staff training to support efficient
production and supply chain operations.

THIRD-PARTY PAYMENT
Background
During the Track Record Period, a small number of our customers (the “Relevant
Customer(s)”) settled their payments with us through third-party payors (the “Third-Party
Payor(s)”), where our customers, Third-Party Payor and our Group had entered into a
tripartite agreement agreeing to such arrangement prior to the payment by the Third-Party
Payor as part of our precautionary measures (the “Third-Party Payment Arrangement(s)”).
We believe our Third-Party Payment Arrangements present relatively low risk considering
that the tripartite agreement structure among the relevant parties established clear payment
obligations, supporting documents and payment instructions, which significantly reduced
counterparty and collection risks compared with informal payment arrangements. These
arrangements arose primarily because certain customers (i) lacked the required import or
foreign-exchangesettlementqualificationsand(ii)usedaffiliatedtradingentitiesforpayment
processing. The number of Relevant Customers was two, three and five in 2023, 2024 and
2025, respectively, and the number of Third-Party Payors was one, two and four for the same
respective periods. The aggregate amount of third-party payments (the “Third-Party
Payments”) received was RMB1.4 million, RMB11.8 million and RMB11.7 million in 2023,
2024and2025,respectively,whichaccountedfor0.02%,0.13%and0.11%of ourtotalrevenue
for the same respective periods. No individual Relevant Customer made a material
contribution to our revenue during the Track Record Period. To the best knowledge of our
Directors, none of the Relevant Customers or their respective Third-Party Payors had any
pastorpresentrelationship(whetherbusiness,employment,family,trust,fundflow,financing
or otherwise) with us, our subsidiaries, shareholders, directors or senior management, or any
of theirrespectiveassociates.DuringtheTrackRecordPeriodanduptotheLatestPracticable
Date, we had not received any claims from Third-Party Payors or their liquidators.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, other than
accepting payments under the Third-Party Payment Arrangements, we had not proactively
initiated any Third-Party Payment Arrangements, nor had we participated in any other form
of such arrangements. In addition, during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest
Practicable Date, we had not provided any discount, commission, rebate or other benefits to
any of the Relevant Customers or the Third-Party Payors to facilitate or encourage the
Third-Party Payment Arrangements. The payment, the pricing terms and other general
commercial terms of the Relevant Customers are generally the same as our other customers.
As advised by our PRC Legal Advisor, our Third-Party Payment Arrangements do not
contravene any prohibitive provisions under PRC laws and regulations. During the Track
RecordPeriodanduptotheLatestPracticableDate,asconfirmedbytheDirectors,(i)wehad
not encountered any disputes with, or received any refund request from, any Relevant
Customer or Third-Party Payor, and (ii) we had not been subject to any disputes or
administrative penalties by the relevant government authorities with respect to the
Third-party Payment Arrangements.
Our Directors have confirmed that, during the Track Record Period and up to the
Latest Practicable Date, (i) all the Third-Party Payments were related to genuine transactions
between us and the Relevant Customers and were made by bank transfers; (ii) the amount of
Third-Party Payments received by us from Third-Party Payors corresponded with the
transaction amount in the relevant sales orders, records and/or invoices between the Relevant
Customers and us; (iii) all relevant transactions involving Third-Party Payments were

Internal Control Measures for Third-Party Payment Arrangements
To safeguard us against risks associated with Third-Party Payment Arrangements, we
have enhanced our internal control measures, including: (i) evaluating Customers effectively,
thereby preventing fraud or money laundering activities, to ensure transaction integrity. We
conduct rigorous screenings of the qualifications of Third-Party Payors to ensure identity
authenticity; and (ii) informing our employees of the risks of third-party payment
arrangements and our strengthened internal control measures, requiring all our employees to
reject or return any payments made in such arrangements that do not comply with the
aforementioned procedures. We plan to cease Third-Party Payment Arrangements before the
ListingandprohibitThird-PartyPaymentArrangementsgoingforward.Specifically,wehave
requested the Relevant Customers to obtain the necessary import and export or
foreign-exchange settlement qualifications, and to make direct payments to us. If any
Relevant Customer was reluctant to obtain such certificates, we would cease transacting with
them.
Considering that our revenue generated from Third-Party Payment Arrangements as a
percentage of our total revenue was immaterial, our Directors confirm that the Third-Party
PaymentArrangementswouldnothaveanymaterialadverseimpactonourbusiness,financial
condition or results of operations.
QUALITY CONTROL
We strictly comply with the Product Quality Law of the PRC. We have established a
comprehensive quality management system and formulated the Quality Manual. We are
certified in accordance with the standards required under ISO9001, ISO14001, ISO45001,
QC080000 and IATF16949. Our products undergo rigorous testing and validation to ensure
that they meet industry standards and customer requirements. As of December 31, 2025, we
had 267 employees responsible for quality control, overseeing system audits, supplier
management, product analysis and continual improvement.
Our quality control process covers technology development, procurement, production,
storage and delivery. We control variation through structured planning, inspect incoming
materials,managesupplierqualityandconductinternalauditstoensureconsistentworkflows
and training compliance. During production, we monitor process trends, identify
abnormalities and implement corrective actions using statistical methods, while engineering
changes are managed through staged validation and reliability checks. We document and
address factory issues, maintain environmental stability and focus on product reliability
throughout development and mass production. We also review customer feedback and, in
massproduction,workwithcustomerstosetyieldanddefectidentificationrequirementsand
jointly analyze testing data to drive continual improvement.

ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
We are committed to sustainable development and continuously enhance our

ESG Governance
ESG Governance Structure
Our Board of Directors bears overall responsibility for our ESG matters. Recognizing
the importance of ESG to our corporate development, the Board has established a Strategy
and ESG Committee and formulated the Working Rules of the Strategy and ESG Committee
(《戰略與ESG委員會工作規則》),whichassignsthecommitteeresponsibilityforreviewingour
development strategies, researching ESG-related issues and making recommendations to the
Board. The committee convenes annually to review ESG topics.
WehavealsoestablishedanESGImplementationCommittee,reportingtotheStrategy
and ESG Committee, which is responsible for integrating and coordinating ESG
implementation across our Company. The ESG Implementation Committee consists of three
working groups, each responsible for promoting environmental protection, energy
conservation and carbon reduction, fulfilling social responsibilities and improving corporate
governance across various departments. Each working group is led by the supervisor of the

Climate Risk Identification and Management
We have established systems to assess climate change risks on our operations, supply
chain and market, and formulated corresponding response and contingency plans. We also
operate a carbon management committee that promotes energy conservation and
consumption reduction, sets annual emission reduction targets and conducts annual carbon
emission verifications.
We face transition and physical risks, including rising compliance and operational
costs, reduced supplier capacity, extreme weather and long-term temperature increases
affecting efficiency and production, which we mitigate through emergency drills, prevention
mechanisms, and preparation of emergency power and water supplies, supported by
ISO-based Environment, Safety and Health (“ESH”) management, environmental
technologies, improved recycling and supplier ESG audits. We also identify climate-related
opportunities such as improved efficiency, reduced costs, increased product demand,
expanded markets, enhanced resilience and the adoption of energy-saving technologies and
new energy vehicle chips, together with enhanced environmental disclosure and strengthened
climate risk and opportunity management.

TARIFF, TRADE RESTRICTION AND EXPORT CONTROL IMPLICATIONS
U.S. Tariff Implications
On December 23, 2025, USTR announced that it would increase the Section 301 Tariff
onChinesesemiconductorimports,withaninitialtariff levelof zero,increasingin18months
on June 23, 2027, to a rate to be announced not fewer than 30 days prior to that date. On
February 1, 2025, President Trump imposed a 10% IEEPA Tariff on all products imported to
the U.S. from China. On April 2, 2025, President Trump imposed a two-tier reciprocal tariff
(the “Reciprocal Tariff”, and together with the Section 301 Tariff and the IEEPA Tariff, the
“Tariffs”) on approximately 60 countries, including China, which consists of a baseline tariff
of 10% and additional individualized tariffs based on each country’s trade deficits with the
U.S. After several rounds of adjustments, the 10% Reciprocal Tariff on goods imported from
China remained but the additional 24% tariff had been suspended until 12:01 a.m. eastern
standard time on November 10, 2026. Following the U.S. Supreme Court’s ruling and
according to the executive orders and notices issued by the U.S. government, the tariffs
imposed under the IEEPA became inactive on February 24, 2026, and instead a temporary
10% tariff is imposed for a period of 150 days. Accordingly, the new U.S. tariff after
cancelling the tariffs under the IEEPA is 10% on goods imported from China as of the Latest
Practicable Date and may be subject to further changes.

U.S. Export Control Implications
Under the EAR, a license from the BIS may be required for the export, re-export or
in-country transfer of any items (including commodities, software and technology) subject to
the EAR. Items subject to the EAR include not only those made in or located within the
United States, but also certain foreign-made items. In addition, recent developments under
the EAR, including the “Supercomputer and Semiconductor Manufacturing End-Use”
restrictions, among others, are designed to limit China’s access to advanced computing and
semiconductor manufacturing technologies. Effective from October 2022, Section 744.23 of
the EAR imposes license requirements where an exporter, re-exporter or transferor knows or
has reason to know that certain EAR-controlled items are intended for supercomputer or
semiconductor manufacturing end-uses, with implementation phased in over time.

International Sanctions Implications
The BIS publishes various trade restriction lists identifying persons, entities or
governments subject to specific license requirements for the export or transfer of designated
items. The principal sanctions list maintained by the OFAC is the SDN List, which includes
persons determined by the U.S. government to be involved in activities that threaten or
undermineU.S.nationalsecurityorforeignpolicyobjectives.Assetsof personsdesignatedon
the SDN List are blocked, and U.S. persons are generally prohibited from dealing with them.
Our U.S. Export Control and Sanctions Legal Advisor is of the view that our Group’s
business, especially dealings with our counterparties, including customers and suppliers,
during the Track Record Period did not constitute Primary Sanctioned Activities or
Secondary Sanctionable Activities, as: (i) we have several domestic offices in Chinese
Mainland and one research center in Japan, none of which are located, incorporated,
organized or domiciled in countries or regions subject to comprehensive sanctions
administered by the Relevant Sanctions Authorities; (ii) neither our Company nor any of our
subsidiaries or respective, respective shareholders is a Sanctioned Target or located in
countries or regions subject to comprehensive sanctions administered by the Relevant
Sanctions Authorities; and (iii) our Company is not owned 50% or more or controlled by any
nationals of the Relevant Jurisdictions.
Based on the counterparty screening conducted since 2019, three of our customers (the
“RelevantCustomers”)arelistedontheBISEntityListwithoutanyfootnotedesignation,and
eleven suppliers (the “Relevant Suppliers”) are also listed on the BIS Entity List. The
aggregate sales revenue generated from Relevant Customers amounted to approximately
RMB103.5 thousand, nil and nil in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively, representing less than
0.1% of our total revenue in each year during the Track Record Period. The aggregate
procurement costs incurred by us in respect of the Relevant Suppliers amounted to
approximately RMB167.4 million, RMB281.2 million and RMB1,228.9 million in 2023, 2024
and2025,respectively,representingapproximately0.9%,2.5%and9.1%of ourtotalcostsfor
the same respective periods. The transaction amounts involved were insignificant, and no
exports or transfers of items subject to the EAR occurred with the Relevant Customers.
Likewise, our procurements from the Relevant Suppliers did not involve any items subject to
the EAR and were not prohibited under applicable export control regulations.
Although the transaction amounts mentioned above were insignificant, we recognize
thatif itemssoldorprocuredbytheGroupweretobecomesubjecttotheEARandadditional
licensing requirements, prohibitions or restrictions as a result of Entity List designations or
broader export control regimes, our ability to supply services or procure certain items could
be affected. Accordingly, notwithstanding the limited scale of the historical transactions, we
have exercised caution in conducting transactions with the Relevant Customers and Relevant
Suppliers to ensure ongoing compliance with applicable export control requirements. To
mitigate potential risks arising from transactions with Relevant Customers and Relevant
Suppliers, we conduct export control checks, comply with supplier and customer trade
requirements, monitor regulatory changes with external advisors and maintain diversified
customer and supplier bases to reduce reliance on any counterpart subject to heightened
controls.
Our Directors are of the view that, taking into account the limited scale of the
transactions involved, our established compliance framework and diversified counterparties,
our exposure to risks arising from trade restrictions and sanctions is manageable and is not
expected to have a material adverse impact on our business operations or financial
performance.Wewillcontinuetostrengthenourcompliancesystems,monitorregulatoryand

and external advisors to ensure ongoing compliance with applicable export control and

Social Insurance and Housing Provident Funds
During the Track Record Period, we did not make social insurance and housing
provident fund contributions for our Non-Chinese Mainland Employees, primarily because
most of our Taiwanese employees preferred to participate in the labor and health insurance
schemes in Taiwan, China. Accordingly, we engaged a third-party human resources agency to
facilitate such contributions in Taiwan, China. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, the shortfall of our
social insurance amounted to RMB19.3 million, RMB19.2 million and RMB18.7 million,
respectively, and the shortfall of our housing provident contributions amounted to RMB5.6
million, RMB5.6 million and RMB5.7 million, respectively. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, the
amount paid by the third-party human resource agency amounted to RMB8.5 million,
RMB8.2 million and RMB8.1 million, respectively.
OurPRCLegalAdvisoradvisesusthat,pursuanttorelevantPRClawsandregulations,
if we fail to pay the full amount of social insurance contributions as required, we may be
ordered to pay the outstanding social insurance contributions within a prescribed time limit
and may be subject to a late payment fee equal to 0.05% of the outstanding contribution
amount for each day of delay. If such payment is not made within the stipulated period, the
competent authority may further impose a fine of one to three times the amount of any
overdue payment. Our PRC Legal Advisor has further advised us that, pursuant to relevant
PRC laws and regulations, government authorities encourage enterprises to contribute to the
housing provident fund for Non-Chinese Mainland employees, but there is no mandatory
requirement to do so. As advised by our PRC Legal Advisor, under the Regulations on the
Administration of Housing Provident Fund promulgated in 2002 and amended in 2019, the
term “employees” refers to staff members who establish labor relationships with employers
within the PRC. According to the policy clarification issued by the Ministry of Construction
in 2006, foreign nationals as well as residents of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan are not
regarded as “employees” for the purposes of the aforesaid Regulations and therefore do not
fallwithinthescopeof mandatoryhousingprovidentfundparticipation.Subsequentpolicies
issued by relevant PRC authorities have further clarified that foreign nationals and residents
of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan who are legally employed in the PRC may, on a voluntary
basis, participate in the housing provident fund scheme and enjoy treatment comparable to
that of PRC nationals if they elect to do so. Such policies reflect a facilitative and supportive
approach but do not impose any compulsory obligation on employers to make housing
provident fund contributions for Non-Chinese Mainland employees. Accordingly, under the
prevailing PRC legal and regulatory framework, employers are not subject to a mandatory
requirement to contribute to the housing provident fund for Non-Chinese Mainland
employees.
Therefore, the housing provident fund authorities will not require us to make
retroactive contributions for such employees. If the payment is not made within such time
limit, an application may be made to the PRC courts for compulsory enforcement. Based on
interviews with the relevant competent authorities, if we settle the shortfall in our
contributions to the social insurance and the relevant late fees within the time frame
stipulated by the relevant competent authorities, the risk of administrative penalties being
imposed on us by the relevant competent authorities is remote.
Our PRC Legal Advisor has conducted independent searches, and confirmed that we
had not been subject to any administrative penalties for failure to pay the full amount of
socialinsurancecontributionsorhousingprovidentfundinaccordancewiththerelevantlaws
and regulations during the Track Record Period. Furthermore, our PRC Legal Advisor’s
searches of publicly available information revealed no instances where social insurance or
housing provident fund authorities required us to make full retroactive payments for all
– 147 –

=== PAGE 157 ===
BUSINESS
employees due to individual employee complaints or reports. Additionally, our PRC Legal
Advisor’sinterviewedwiththerelevantcompetentauthorities,whohadconfirmedthat(i)the
likelihood of penalties is remote if we promptly make up any shortfall in contributions and
late payment fees upon request; (ii) even in the event of an employee complaint regarding
social insurance, the authorities are unlikely to mandate full payments for the historical
amounts; and (iii) for housing provident fund complaints, mediation procedures would
precede any investigation. Moreover, as advised by our PRC Legal Advisor based on the
aforementioned, in the absence of material employee complaints, the likelihood of being
subject to material administrative penalties or collection of historical arrears is remote. As a
result,wehadnotrectifiedsuchshortfallnormadeanyprovisionfortheshortfallinoursocial
insurance and housing provident fund contributions during the Track Record Period and up

Furthermore, as advised by our PRC Legal Advisor, in light of Article 19(1) of the
Interpretation (II) by the Supreme People’s Court of Issues Concerning the Application of
Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases《( 最高人民法院關於審理勞動爭議案件適用法律問題
的解釋（二）》) (“Interpretation”) promulgated by the Supreme People’s Court of the PRC on
July 31, 2025 and which took effect on September 1, 2025, if an employer and an employee
agree or the employee undertakes that social insurance contributions need not be paid, the
People’s Court shall deem such agreement or undertaking invalid. Furthermore, where an
employer fails to pay social insurance contributions in accordance with the law, and the
employee seeks to terminate the labor contract and claims economic compensation from the
employer pursuant to Article 38(3) of the PRC Labor Contract Law, the People’s Court shall
support such claims, in which case, the employer remains liable for paying economic
compensation (calculated as the number of years of employment multiplied by the monthly
salary) to the employee, notwithstanding any prior agreement to waive social insurance
contributions.See“RegulatoryOverview—RegulationsonLaborandEmployment—Social
Insurance and Housing Provident Fund.”
Our Directors are of the view, and the PRC Legal Advisor concurs, that, the
Interpretation will not have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition or
results of operations, taking into account that: (i) the implementation of the Interpretation
will not affect our compliance status with respect to social insurance and housing provident
fund contributions, as the aforementioned judicial interpretation does not repeal the social
insurance laws and regulations currently in force of the PRC; (ii) the Interpretation does not
create any new basis for reassessing contribution shortfalls or exposing us to increased
penalties; (iii) no employee has brought a lawsuit or arbitration in respect of payment of
social insurance and therefore no pending litigation or arbitration of our Company is
applicable to the aforementioned judicial interpretations; and (iv) any shortfall in social
insurance or housing provident fund contributions has been accounted for in our shortfall
calculations.Onsuchbasis,nothinghascometotheattentionof theSoleSponsorthatwould
causetheSoleSponsortodisagreewiththeviewsof theDirectorsandthePRCLegalAdvisor
above.
We have strengthened our internal controls by enhancing our human resource
management policies to ensure that social insurance and housing provident fund
contributions strictly follow local requirements, improving staff training on compliance
matters and regularly monitoring updates in PRC laws and regulations. In addition, we
consultourPRClegalcounselandmaintainactivecommunicationwithlocalsocialinsurance
and housing fund authorities to stay informed of regulatory developments and ensure

INTERNAL CONTROL PROCEDURES ADOPTED TO SAFEGUARD SHAREHOLDERS’
INTERESTS
Inordertofurthersafeguardtheinterestsof theShareholdersasawhole(includingthe
minority Shareholders), our Group has implemented the following internal control measures
in relation to the continuing connected transactions:
• we have adopted a connected transactions management policy for the purpose of
ensuring that our connected transactions will be conducted in a fair manner, on
normal commercial terms and in the interests of our Company and our
Shareholders as a whole.
• priortotheexecutionof theconnectedtransactions,thefunctiondepartmentsof
our Group will compare the terms of the proposed transactions (including
pricingandothercontractualterms)withthosesimilartransactionsenteredwith
Independent Third Parties or the terms offered to Independent Third Parties (as
the case may be) to ensure that the terms of such connected transactions shall be
no less favorable to our Group than those offered by our Group to Independent
Third Parties.
• we will regularly review the terms of our continuing connected transactions, in
particular, the prices from the connected persons, research in prevailing market
conditionsandpracticesand,whereapplicable,makereferencetothepricingand
terms between our Company and Independent Third Parties for similar
transactions to ensure they are on normal commercial terms and are fair and
reasonable.
• our independent non-executive Directors and auditors will conduct annual
review of the continuing connected transactions entered into by our Company
and provide annual confirmations in accordance with Rules 14A.55 and 14A.56
of the Listing Rules, and our Company will provide information and supporting
documents to the independent non-executive Directors and the auditors to
facilitate their annual review.
• When considering any renewal or revisions to the agreements after the Listing,
the interested Directors and Shareholders shall abstain from voting on the
resolutions to approve such transactions at board meetings or shareholders’
general meetings (as the case may be). If the independent Directors’ or
independent Shareholders’ approvals cannot be obtained, we will not continue
the transactions under the framework agreement(s) to the extent that they
constitute non-exempt continuing connected transactions under rule 14A.35 of
the Listing Rules.
WAIVER
In respect of the non-exempt continuing connected transactions as described above, we
haveappliedfor,andtheStockExchangehasgrantedus,awaiverfromstrictcompliancewith

Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules in respect of the continuing connected transactions as
disclosed in “— Non-exempt continuing connected transactions subject to reporting, annual
review,announcement,circularandindependentShareholders’approvalrequirements”inthis
section; and (ii) the announcement requirement under Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules in
respect of the continuing connected transactions as disclosed in “— Non-exempt continuing
connected transactions subject to reporting, annual review and announcement requirements”
in this section, subject to the condition that the aggregate amounts of such continuing
connected transactions for each financial year shall not exceed the relevant amounts set forth
in the annual caps (as stated above).

NON-COMPETE UNDERTAKINGS
In connection with our A-Shares listing, each of Hefei Construction Investment and
Hefei Xinping (the “Undertaking Shareholder(s)”) has provided a non-compete undertaking
(the “Non-compete Undertaking”) to our Company in April 2021 in order to avoid potential
competition, pursuant to which, each of the Undertaking Shareholders has undertaken that,
among others:
(1) as of the date of the Non-compete Undertaking, the Undertaking Shareholder
and other enterprises directly or indirectly controlled by it do not, and will not,
whether within or outside China, in any manner, directly or indirectly engage in
any business that are the same as or similar to the principal business of the
Company and its subsidiaries;
(2) for any future circumstances where the Undertaking Shareholder and other
enterprises directly or indirectly controlled by it engage in any business that are
the same as or similar to the principal business of the Company and its
subsidiaries, the Undertaking Shareholder and any enterprises directly or
indirectly controlled by it shall: (a) be willing to transfer the assets or equity
interests (if any) relating to such competing business to the Company or its
subsidiaries at a fair and reasonable price, (b) grant the Company a pre-emptive
right to acquire such assets or equity interests, and (c) if the Company for any
reasondecidesnottoexercisesuchrightandnotifytheUndertakingShareholder
promptly, the Undertaking Shareholder and other enterprises directly or
indirectlycontrolledbyitshalleitherceasesuchcompetingbusinessordivestthe
relevant assets or equity interests to eliminate control;
(3) if in the future, any business opportunities available to the Undertaking
ShareholderandotherenterprisesmaycompetewiththeCompany’sbusiness,the
Undertaking Shareholder and other enterprises directly or indirectly controlled
by it shall notify the Company and use best efforts to ensure that such
opportunity is first offered to the Company or its subsidiaries. The Company or

INDEPENDENCE FROM OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS GROUP
Our Directors consider that we are capable of carrying on our business independently
from our Controlling Shareholders Group and their respective close associates after the
Listing, taking into consideration the factors below.
Management Independence
Our Board consists of nine Directors, including two executive Directors, four
non-executive Directors and three independent non-executive Directors. Three of our
non-executive Directors, namely, Mr. LU Qinhang, Ms. CHEN Xiaobei and Mr. GUO
Zhaozhi, hold directorship or managerial positions within Hefei Construction Investment.
Our Directors consider that we are capable of maintaining management independence
for the following reasons:
(a) save for Mr. LU Qinhang, Ms. CHEN Xiaobei and Mr. GUO Zhaozhi, none of
our Directors or members of our senior management team holds any position in
our Controlling Shareholders or their respective close associates. Each of LU
Qinhang,Ms.CHENXiaobeiandMr.GUOZhaozhiisanon-executiveDirector,
andisnotinvolvedintheday-to-daymanagementandbusinessoperationsof our
Group;
(b) our daily management and operations are carried out independently by our
seniormanagementteam,allof whomhavesubstantialexperienceintheindustry
in which our Company is engaged, and will therefore be able to make business
decisions that are in the best interests of our Company;
(c) each Director is aware of his/her fiduciary duties as a director which require,
among other things, that he/she acts for the benefit and in the interest of our
Company and does not allow any conflict between his/her duties as a Director
and his/her personal interests;
(d) in the event that there is a potential conflict of interest arising out of any
transaction to be entered into between our Company and a Director and/or
his/her associate, he/she shall abstain from voting and shall not be counted
towards the quorum for the voting. Hence, no Director will be able to influence
our Board in making decisions on matters in which he or she is, or may be
interested; and
(e) we have three independent non-executive Directors and certain matters of our
Company, including continuing connected transactions, must always be referred
to the independent non-executive Directors for review. We have adopted a series
of corporategovernancemeasurestomanageconflictsof interest,if any,between
ourCompanyandourControllingShareholdersGroupwhichwouldsupportour
independent management. See “— Corporate Governance”for details.
Based on the above, our Directors believe that our Board as a whole and together with
our senior management are able to perform the managerial role in our Company
independently from our Controlling Shareholders and their respective close associates after
the Listing.

OVERVIEW
Wearealeadingpure-playfoundryspecializingin12-inchwafermanufacturing,operating
at a critical juncture of the global semiconductor value chain. As dedicated wafer fabrication
service providers, foundries translate IC design blueprints from fabless, fablite and integrated
devicemanufacturer(“IDM”)companiesintohigh-qualityprocessedwafersatscale.
Since inception, we have focused on the advancement of process technologies. Our
foundry services cover technology nodes ranging from 150nm to 40nm, with the 28nm Logic
IC platform successfully developed as of the Latest Practicable Date, positioning us to
address evolving demand for higher-performance and more power-efficient semiconductor
solutions. Our process capabilities are centered on key application-specific IC categories,
including display driver ICs (“DDIC”) that enable display control, complementary
metal-oxide-semiconductor image sensors (“CIS”) that enable image sensing, and power
management ICs (“PMIC”) that regulate and optimize power usage. Our Logic ICs, which
support data processing, and microcontroller units (“MCU”), which provide embedded
control, have also scaled rapidly during the Track Record Period. Leveraging this portfolio,
we are able to support a broad spectrum of applications across consumer electronics,
automotiveelectronics,industrialcontrol,artificialintelligence(“AI”),theInternetof Things
(“IoT”) and memory.
Our ability to combine differentiated process technologies with stable manufacturing
scale has strengthened our position in the global foundry landscape. From 2020 to 2025, we
achieved the fastest growth in production capacity and revenue among the global top ten
wafer foundries, according to Frost & Sullivan. In 2025, we ranked as the ninth largest wafer
foundry worldwide and the third largest in Chinese Mainland by revenue, according to the
same source.
WehaveconsistentlydemonstratedstablegrowthamidindustrycyclesduringtheTrack
Record Period. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our total revenue amounted to RMB7,182.7 million,
RMB9,119.6 million and RMB10,388.3 million, respectively, with gross profit margins of
20.3%, 25.2% and 22.7% in the same respective years. Our net profit was RMB119.2 million,
RMB482.2millionandRMB466.5millionin2023,2024and2025,respectively,withnetprofit
margins of 1.7%, 5.3% and 4.5% in the same respective years.

MAJOR FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
We believe that a number of factors directly or indirectly affect our business, financial
condition and results of operations, including the following general factors that affect our
industry as a whole, some of which are beyond our control:
• overall economic growth and conditions;
• the competitive landscape and market demand in our industry;
• relevant laws and regulations, government policies and initiatives; and
• the occurrence of force majeure events, the outbreak of pandemics or epidemics,
acts of war, social and economic chaos and natural disasters.
In addition, our business, financial condition and results of operations have been, and
are expected to be, continuously affected by a number of industry- and company-specific
factors, including the following:
Cyclicality of the Semiconductor Industry
The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical mainly due to fluctuations in global
end-marketdemandforproductsthatusesemiconductors,thelongleadtimesassociatedwith
capacity expansion and the capital-intensive nature of production. During upturns, industry
participants typically expand capacity through substantial capital investments in new
production facilities and equipment. As such capacity is brought into operation, it often
results in periods of oversupply and downward pressure on prices. Conversely, during supply
shortages, foundries generally benefit from improved pricing and higher utilization rates. The
semiconductor industry is generally slow to react to declines in demand due to its
capital-intensive nature and the long lead times for equipment in advance of the planned
expansion. See “Industry Overview — Global Wafer Foundry Market — The Size of Global
Wafer Foundry Market.”
We have achieved stable growth amid the cyclical dynamics of the semiconductor
industry. Our total revenue increased from RMB7,182.7 million in 2023 to RMB9,119.6
million in 2024, and continued to grow to RMB10,388.3 million in 2025. While we cannot
eliminate the impact of cyclical fluctuations, we believe our focus on 12-inch wafer
fabrication, broad coverage across multiple product categories and sustained investment in
technology advancement enhance our resilience against industry downturns. By aligning our
technology platforms with long-term demand drivers such as high-resolution displays,
advanced imaging, automotive electronics and power management, we are well positioned to
capture growth opportunities as market conditions recover.

Customer Relationships and Diversification of Our Customer Base
Our ability to maintain strong customer relationships and expand our customer base is
critical to our future business growth. Supported by our production capabilities, we have
established ourselves as a trusted foundry partner for customers. In 2025, our revenue from
Chinese Mainland and countries/regions outside of Chinese Mainland accounted for 61.4%
and38.6%of ourtotalrevenue,respectively.Throughclosecollaborationwithourcustomers,
we have developed a stable and frequent communication mechanism, which enables us to
obtain accurate and timely feedback on customer needs, gain deep insights into core
requirements, product trends and the latest technology demands, and ensure our foundry
technologies are continuously updated and aligned with market developments.
To further capture new business opportunities and reduce reliance on any single
customer or market segment, we have continued to optimize our offerings in line with end
market needs and expand our customer base, attracting both leading global companies and
emerging industry players in high-growth sectors such as consumer electronics, automotive
electronics,micro-displaysandAI.Inaddition,wemaintainastructuredsalesandmarketing
framework that integrates rigorous market analysis with targeted outreach, enabling us to
recommendtailoredtechnologyplatformsandfoundrysolutionsthatmeettheevolvingneeds
of diverse customer segments. We believe that our strong customer relationships, combined
with our ongoing efforts to broaden our customer portfolio, can enhance our ability to
navigate industry cycles and position us to capture growth opportunities sustainably.
Supply Chain and Production Capacity Management
Maintaining a stable supply chain and flexible production capacity is fundamental to
our sustained business operations and growth. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, the raw materials
consumedunderthecostof salesamountedtoRMB1,926.4million,RMB2,416.7millionand
RMB2,725.9 million, respectively, representing 33.7%, 35.4% and 33.9% of our total cost of
sales in the same respective years. We have established a comprehensive supply chain
management system and continually enhanced our supply chain security by actively
promoting the localization of key materials and equipment, maximizing the use of locally
sourced resources to strengthen resilience and mitigate supply chain risks.
In addition, we maintain an adaptable production capacity management system that
centers around customer demand. We regularly review production utilization, optimize
processes and upgrade equipment to unlock additional capacity and respond swiftly to
evolvingcustomerneeds.Inparallel,wedynamicallyadjustorderintakebasedonproduction
utilization and product lead times to enhance our overall profitability. Our intelligent
manufacturingsystemsfurtherfacilitateefficientresourceallocationandscalableproduction,
ensuring consistently high throughput and stable, high-quality output across diverse product
lines and complex process flows. During the Track Record Period, we had production
utilization rates of 72.5%, 94.0% and 100.8% in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. By
deepening localization efforts, diversifying strategic partnerships with suppliers and further
investing in intelligent production systems, we aim to proactively mitigate potential risks and
respond swiftly to market dynamics. Such ongoing initiatives will underpin our ability to
deliver stable, high-quality output and support the sustainable growth of our business.
Continual Advancement and Optimization of our Technology Platform
The foundry industry is characterized by rapid innovation cycles, evolving customer
requirements and the constant emergence of new applications, all of which necessitate
ongoingR&Dinvestmentandcontinualoptimizationof ourtechnologyplatforms.Supported
by our experienced R&D team, we have established mass production capabilities across
mainstream technology nodes from 150nm to 40nm, and had completed the development of
28nm Logic IC platforms as of the Latest Practicable Date. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our
research and development expenses amounted to RMB1,057.5 million, RMB1,284.0 million
and RMB1,453.4 million, respectively, sustainably driving the iterative innovation of our
technology platforms and specialized production technologies.
– 184 –

=== PAGE 194 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
In addition, the value of a wafer is primarily determined by the complexity and
performances of the process technology used in its production, as well as by the yield
achieved. Fabricating devices with higher levels of functionality and performance, better
yields and greater system-level integration requires more advanced production expertise and
generally commands higher wafer prices. Typically, once an appropriate economy of scale is
achieved, the price increases for wafers processed with more advanced technologies will
outweigh the corresponding increases in unit production costs. As such, the mix of wafers we
producedrivenbyongoingupgradesanddiversificationof ourtechnologyplatformsremains
a primary factor affecting our revenue and profitability. We have continued to invest in
high-growth applications, such as BSI and full-process stacked CIS, Micro OLED DDIC for
AR/VR devices, automotive-grade DDICs and MCUs, as well as technology platforms to
support next-generation applications in consumer electronics, smart vehicles, micro-displays
and AI, among others. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we were actively advancing the
development of our 28nm technology platforms and had commenced pilot run of our 28nm
Logic IC platform. These advancements are expected to significantly enhance our product
performance, integration density and power efficiency, enabling us to capture incremental
demand from high-end markets and improve overall profitability.
Looking ahead, we anticipate that the ongoing advancement and robust growth of
downstream industries, including consumer electronics, automotive electronics, smart home,
industrial control, AI, the IoT and memory, will continue to drive strong demand for
advanced and diversified IC wafer manufacturing services. We remain committed to further
increasing our investment in R&D and to the continual optimization of our technology
platforms, reinforcing our leadership in core technology platforms, strengthening our
competitive position and supporting sustainable revenue growth amid the ongoing
transformation of the global semiconductor landscape.

fiveyears,pursuanttorelevantPRCtaxincentivesforqualifiedenterprises.Therefore,during
the Track Record Period and up to 2026, the effective tax rate of our Company and Hefei
Xinjing was, and will remain, zero. From 2027 to 2031, our Company and Hefei Xinjing will
be eligible for a preferential tax rate of 12.5%. In addition, they are expected to benefit from
a further five-year exemption from corporate income tax from 2027 to 2031, pursuant to the
relevant PRC tax incentives available to qualified enterprises. During the Track Record
Period, all income tax expenses were attributable to our subsidiary in Japan. See Note 11 to
the Accountants’Report in Appendix I to this Prospectus.
YEAR-TO-YEAR COMPARISON OF RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Year Ended December 31, 2025 Compared with Year Ended December 31, 2024
Revenue
Our revenue increased by 13.9% from RMB9,119.6 million in 2024 to RMB10,388.3
millionin2025,primarilyduetoanincreaseinrevenuefromsalesof productsbasedonourIC
wafer foundry services, mainly driven by the increase in market demand for CIS and PMIC
products and customers’growing recognition of our quality foundry solutions.
Cost of Sales
Our cost of sales increased by 17.7% from RMB6,820.2 million in 2024 to RMB8,030.2
million in 2025, primarily due to (i) an increase in depreciation and amortization, mainly
relating to the increase in machinery and equipment in line with our ongoing production
expansion, and (ii) an increase in raw material consumed, corresponding with the growth in
our production and sales volume.
Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
Our gross profit increased by 2.6% from RMB2,299.3 million in 2024 to RMB2,358.1
million in 2025. Our gross profit margin decreased from 25.2% in 2024 to 22.7% in 2025,
primarily because we had intensified efforts to diversify our technology platforms and drive
salesgrowthof newproductlinessince2024.Thesenewproductsarestillintheramp-upstage
andhavenotyetachievedsufficienteconomiesof scale,resultinginagrossprofitmarginthat
is slightly lower than that of our more mature products, such as DDIC.
Other Income
Our other income increased by 45.1% from RMB327.3 million in 2024 to RMB475.0
millionin2025,primarilyduetotherecognitionof atechnologytransferincomeinrelationto
ourphotomasktechnologytransferin2025,partiallyoffsetbythedecreaseininterestincome
in line with the decreases in our bank deposits.
Other Gains, Net
We recorded net other gains of RMB4.5 million in 2025 as compared to net other gains
of RMB71.8millionin2024,primarilydueto(i)thenetforeignexchangelossesasaresultof
fluctuations in exchange rates, and (ii) the decreases in investment income of structured
deposits, transferable large denomination certificates of deposits and income certificates
attributable to a decrease in our overall holdings of these investments. This was partially
offset by the fair value changes on financial assets at FVTPL, mainly attributable to (i) the
purchase of more transferable large-denomination certificate of deposits in 2025, and (ii) the
fair value gain in listed equity instruments.

Year Ended December 31, 2024 Compared with Year Ended December 31, 2023
Revenue
Our revenue increased by 27.0% from RMB7,182.7 million in 2023 to RMB9,119.6
millionin2024,primarilyduetoanincreaseinrevenuefromsalesof productsbasedonourIC
wafer foundry services. Since the fourth quarter of 2023, with the gradual expansion of
foundry capacity and the normalization of market demand, the need for foundry services
began to increase. See “Industry Overview — Global Wafer Foundry Market — The Size of
Global Wafer Foundry Market.”The growth in our revenue from sales of products based on
our IC wafer foundry services in 2024 was mainly driven by a substantial increase in market
demand for CIS and PMIC products, mainly reflecting their wider adoption in mid- to
high-end smartphones and other consumer electronic products, such as laptops, in-vehicle
cameras and LED screens. Such wider adoption was in line with the overall development of
the consumer electronic products market and the expansion of our customers’market share.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Cost of Sales
Our cost of sales increased by 19.2% from RMB5,722.1 million in 2023 to RMB6,820.2
million in 2024, primarily due to (i) an increase in raw materials consumed, corresponding
with the growth in production and sales volume, and (ii) an increase in depreciation and
amortization,mainlyrelatingtothemachineryandequipmentusedinproductioninlinewith
increased production capacity.
Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
As a result of the foregoing, our gross profit increased by 57.4% from RMB1,460.6
millionin2023toRMB2,299.3millionin2024.Ourgrossprofitmarginincreasedfrom20.3%
in2023to25.2%in2024,primarilyasaresultof theimprovedeconomiesof scaleachievedby
increased customer orders and production volumes, which enabled more efficient utilization
of equipment, utilities and other production resources.
Other Income
Our other income decreased by 22.0% from RMB419.8 million in 2023 to RMB327.3
million in 2024, primarily due to the decrease in interest income in line with the reductions in
our bank deposits and the corresponding interest rates.
Other Gains, Net
Our net other gains decreased by 34.0% from RMB108.8 million in 2023 to RMB71.8
million in 2024, primarily due to (i) a decrease in the investment income of structured
deposits, transferable large-denomination certificates of deposits and income certificates, as
well as a decrease in fair value gains on financial assets at FVTPL, both as a result of a
decrease in our holdings of structured deposits and income certificates in 2024, and (ii) a
decrease in net foreign exchange gains as a result of fluctuations in exchange rates.
Research and Development Expenses
Our research and development expenses increased by 21.4% from RMB1,057.5 million
in 2023 to RMB1,284.0 million in 2024, primarily due to (i) an increase in employee benefit
expenses mainly driven by the increase in the number of R&D staff to support our ongoing
technology improvement initiatives, and (ii) an increase in research and development
materials consumed and research, testing and development fees in line with our continuous
efforts in relation to technology improvement initiatives.
General and Administrative Expenses
Ourgeneralandadministrativeexpensesincreasedby22.1%fromRMB310.6millionin
2023 to RMB379.3 million in 2024, primarily due to (i) an increase in employee benefit
expenses, mainly attributable to the increase in the number of our administrative staff in line
with our business growth, and (ii) an increase in depreciation and amortization related to the
expansion of our office area and the deployment of new office equipment.
Selling Expenses
Our selling expenses increased by 9.3% from RMB50.2 million in 2023 to RMB54.8
million in 2024, primarily due to the increases in the number and salaries of our sales staff in
line with our business growth.
Impairment Losses Reversed on Financial Assets, Net
Our net impairment losses reversed on financial assets increased from RMB0.1 million
in2023toRMB1.8millionin2024,primarilyduetothechangesinoverduebalancesof trade
receivables.

financial assets at fair value through profit or loss decreased by 92.8% from RMB607.4
million as of December 31, 2024 to RMB43.7 million as of December 31, 2025, primarily
because transferable large-denomination certificates of deposits due within one year were
classified as part of the current financial assets at fair value through profit or loss.
Ourcurrentfinancialassetsatfairvaluethroughprofitorlossdecreasedby31.1%from
RMB1,548.4 million as of December 31, 2023 to RMB1,066.1 million as of December 31,
2024, primarily due to the decreases in current structured deposits and income certificates,
partially offset by the increase in current transferable large-denomination certificates of
deposits. Our current financial assets at fair value through profit or loss increased by 61.6%
from RMB1,066.1 million as of December 31, 2024 to RMB1,723.0 million as of December
31, 2025, primarily due to (i) the increases in current transferable large-denomination
certificates of deposits and structured deposits, and (ii) the increase in listed equity
instruments,partiallyoffsetbythedecreaseincurrentincomecertificates,inaccordancewith
our wealth management strategy.
We conduct cash management through our internal policies and guidelines to monitor
and control investment risks. We strategically prioritize to invest idle funds in low-risk,
short-termwealthmanagementproductsofferedbybanks.Wesubmitanannualreporttothe
Board of Directors and the shareholders’ meeting (if needed) detailing a proposal regarding
the cash management. Within the approved investment quota, we utilize idle funds to
purchase wealth management products on a rolling basis while ensuring sufficient working
capital to meet daily operational needs. Any purchase of wealth management products
requiresapprovalbasedonourFinancialOperationsResponsibilityAssignmentSystem(財務
作業權責劃分表) before investments can be made within the authorized limits. This process
takes into consideration multiple factors, including our own working capital status,
investment duration, expected returns and potential losses, among others. Our finance
department plays a crucial role in proposing, analyzing and evaluating potential investment
options in wealth management products and maintains detailed records of each wealth
management product, including the purchase amount, redemptions and returns. Upon the
Listing,totheextentthataninvestmentinfinancialproductsisanotifiabletransactionunder
Chapter14of theListingRules,wewillcomplywiththerelevantrequirementsunderChapter
14 of the Listing Rules, including the announcement, circular, reporting and/or approval
requirements (if applicable).

IMPACT OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
On January 30, 2020, the International Health Regulations Emergency Committee of
the World Health Organization declared the novel coronavirus disease 2019 (the
“COVID-19”) outbreak a public health emergency of international concern, and on March
11,2020,theWorldHealthOrganizationdeclaredtheglobalCOVID-19outbreakapandemic.
During 2022, demand for electronic products such as computers and tablets increased
significantly, driven by remote working and online learning needs, which in turn supported
higher order volumes and pricing, particularly in the DDIC foundry segment. Following this
period of elevated demand, the semiconductor market entered a post_pandemic
normalizationphasein2023,asdownstreamcustomersadjustedinventorylevelsanddemand
dynamics returned to more normalized patterns. See “Industry Overview — Global Wafer
Foundry Market — The Size of Global Integrated Circuit Market.”

USE OF PROCEEDS
We estimate that we will receive net proceeds of approximately HK$6,535.6 million
from the Global Offering, after deducting the underwriting fees and commissions and
estimated expenses payable by us in connection with the Global Offering, assuming the Offer
Priceof HK$31.15perOfferShare(beingthemid-pointof theOfferPricerangeof HK$30.00
toHK$32.30)andassumingthattheOver-allotmentOptionisnotexercised.Weintendtouse
the net proceeds from the Global Offering for the following purposes:
• Approximately 53.6%, or HK$3,503.2 million, of the net proceeds is expected to
be used for the R&D and optimization of next-generation 22nm technology
platformtostrengthenourtechnologicalcompetitivenessandaddressthemarket
demand for high-performance products. In particular:
o Approximately 40.8%, or HK$2,666.5 million, of the net proceeds is
expected to be used for the acquisition and installation of specialized
equipmenttosupporttheR&Dandoptimizationof next-generation22nm
process technology. We plan to use approximately 36.1%, or HK$2,359.4
million, of the net proceeds to procure 42 pieces of key equipment and use
approximately 4.7%, or HK$307.2 million, of the net proceeds to procure
corresponding auxiliary devices for use in our wafer fabrication process in
the following two years.
o Approximately 6.6%, or HK$431.4 million, of the net proceeds is expected
to be used for the procurement of IP and EDA tools to enable the efficient
simulation, verification and tape-out of next-generation 22nm process
technology products in the following two years. In terms of IP, we plan to
use approximately 4.1%, or HK$268.0 million, of the net proceeds to
procure and establish a comprehensive set of foundational and special IP,
such as standard cell library, IO, static random access memory cell and
high speed IP. In terms of EDA tools, we plan to use approximately 2.5%,
or HK$163.4 million, of the net proceeds to introduce simulation,
verification and design checking tools.
o Approximately 4.0%, or HK$261.5 million, of the net proceeds is expected
to be used for: (i) the acquisition of testing equipment to enhance R&D
efficiency and improve yield; (ii) the procurement of critical production
materials, such as silicon wafers and photomasks; and (iii) the purchase of
necessary testing accessories, such as probe cards and modular
components, for testing equipment, in three years.
o Approximately 2.2%, or HK$143.8 million, of the net proceeds is expected
to be used for personnel expenses to support the development of the
next-generation 22nm technology platform. We plan to establish a team of
around 100 R&D specialists in three years with extensive experience in
semiconductor process development, with all core members holding
master’s degrees or higher. The team will be dedicated to optimizing
semiconductor device performance, driving innovation in technology
platform development and implementing rigorous quality testing and
validation procedures.
We believe the plan of the R&D and optimization of next-generation 22nm
technology platform to be reasonable and feasible on the following grounds: (i)
the 22nm process provides a favorable balance of logic density, performance and
cost,makingitsuitableforawiderangeof applicationssuchasautomotive-grade

foundation, as well as our process technology for DDIC, CIS and PMIC, with

R&D pathway for the 22nm platform.
• Approximately 23.1%, or HK$1,509.7 million, of the net proceeds is expected to

spanning the entire process from R&D to production, enabling intelligent

In terms of intelligent production, we plan to use approximately 8.7%, or

an integrated intelligent production system and enhance operational

(i) we plan to procure 51 intelligent production systems, such as an
intelligent early warning and analysis platform, intelligent

machinery and computer vision inference, which will integrate AI

(ii) we plan to procure 44 intelligent equipment systems, such as
intelligent machine monitoring, intelligent parameter adjustment,
intelligent recipe creation and intelligent equipment systems, which
will apply AI and automation technologies to accomplish intelligent

(iii) we plan to procure 53 intelligent management systems, such as

will enhance work efficiency through digital employee center

report analysis.
In terms of intelligent R&D, we plan to use approximately 5.6%, or

related to automated predictive optimization and intelligent defect
detection, such as intelligent yield analysis, intelligent wafer analysis,
intelligent production path prediction, hotspot analysis and AI R&D

in process development, thereby improving the product yield.

ComparedtoR&Dandproductionapproachesthatprimarilyconcentrateonthe
development of specific products or technologies, our intelligent R&D and
production initiatives are committed to building an AI application ecosystem for
R&D and production and leveraging AI technology to drive improvements in
both efficiency and output quality. By investing in software systems and
intelligent hardware, we aim to optimize various stages of the R&D and
production processes, reducing manual intervention and minimizing errors. In
addition, the recruitment of skilled professionals with expertise in AI, industrial
automation and semiconductor R&D will further strengthen our capabilities,
enabling us to accelerate innovation cycles, respond more effectively to market
demands and maintain a competitive edge. This integrated approach is designed
not only to streamline operations but also to continuously enhance our industry
competitiveness.
We believe the plan of intelligent R&D and production initiatives based on AI
technology to be reasonable and feasible on the following grounds: (i) AI-driven
tools have demonstrated the capability to reduce equipment downtime, optimize
resourceallocationandshortenproductioncycles,therebyincreasingthroughput
and lowering unit production costs; and (ii) in addition to embedding AI-driven
intelligent manufacturing throughout our production processes, we have
established a robust framework and clear direction for our intelligent R&D and
production initiatives, and this framework adopts a systematic approach that
integrates intelligent software, advanced hardware and highly skilled
professionals, ensuring the effective and sustainable implementation of AI
technology across our operations.
